<div class="field field--field-rich-text wfp-wrapper clearfix">

        
      <div class="prose field-rich-text--container mv4 mv5-lg">
    <div>
              <p>For decades, Palestine has faced a protracted humanitarian crisis driven by <strong>conflict, displacement, economic decline and restricted access</strong> to resources and services.</p>
<p>The situation deteriorated significantly following a sharp escalation of violence in October 2023, leaving<strong> families across Gaza and the West Bank struggling to meet their basic needs.</strong></p>
<p>Food security in Gaza has improved since a ceasefire was announced in October 2025, chiefly due to large-scale humanitarian assistance.</p>
<p>However, the situation remains extremely fragile. According to the latest <a href="https://www.wfp.org/stories/5-steps-food-security-famine">Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) analysis</a>, <strong>1.4 million people – around two thirds of the population – are experiencing crisis or worse </strong>levels of acute food insecurity. </p>
<p>Many families continue to rely on emergency coping strategies, while access to diverse and nutritious diets remains limited.</p>
<p>However, funding shortages have forced the <strong>World Food Programme (WFP) </strong>to reduce food assistance in Gaza by around one-third – to <strong>1.1 million people </strong>– with <strong>half a million people losing access to critical assistance.</strong> The cuts come as winter approaches and recent modest improvements in food security remain fragile.</p>
<p>Continuing insecurity, restricted humanitarian access, damaged infrastructure, unemployment and limited livelihood opportunities continue to undermine recovery and food security. <strong>If humanitarian assistance is not sustained, food insecurity could rapidly worsen.</strong></p>
<p>In the <strong>West Bank</strong>, increasing violence, displacement and economic hardship are placing additional pressure on vulnerable households. WFP provides<strong> food assistance, cash support, nutrition services and livelihood programmes </strong>to help families withstand the ongoing crisis and build a pathway towards recovery.</p>
<p>However, funding shortfalls mean the <strong>number of people receiving assistance in the West Bank has been cut by a half</strong>, from 400,000 to 200,000.</p>

  <h2 class="page-stripe__title wfp-wrapper">What the World Food Programme is doing in Palestine</h2>
  



<section class="accordion wfp-wrapper">

  <dl class="accordion__items" data-js-hook="accordion__items" data-once="accordion">
          <dt class="accordion__item-title" data-js-hook="accordion__item-title" tabindex="0" aria-controls="accordion-panel-1" aria-expanded="true">
        <div>
          <h3>Food assistance</h3>
        </div>
      </dt>
      <dd class="accordion__item-panel" id="accordion-panel-1" aria-hidden="false">
        <div class="accordion__item-content">Families receiving food assistance in Gaza will now receive only one food parcel (instead of two) and a smaller bag of wheat flour. The number of hot meals WFP provides has been reduced from 250,000 to 150,000 a day. Families living in hard-to-reach areas, including near the yellow line of Israeli military control, will receive a hot meal every other day instead of daily. WFP has also reduced the value of cash assistance provided to 75,000 families in Gaza. For now, WFP is able to continue supporting bakeries that cover one-third of Gaza’s bread needs, provide nutrition assistance to 300,000 women and children and deliver healthy school snacks to 200,000 children.</div>
                  <aside class="accordion__item-side">
                          <div class="accordion__item-image">
                <img src="https://www.wfp.org/sites/default/files/styles/page_accordion/public/images/Palestine-food-assistance-WFP-Mostsfa-Ghroz.jpeg?itok=klPuny9w" alt="Hala, a five-year-old enjoying a freshly baked loaf of bread, made from the wheat flour her mom redeems from the WFP voucher she receives. Photo: WFP/Mostafa Ghroz">
              </div>
                                  </aside>
              </dd>
          <dt class="accordion__item-title" data-js-hook="accordion__item-title" tabindex="0" aria-controls="accordion-panel-2" aria-expanded="false">
        <div>
          <h3>Livelihood support</h3>
        </div>
      </dt>
      <dd class="accordion__item-panel" id="accordion-panel-2" aria-hidden="true" inert="">
        <div class="accordion__item-content">WFP supports livelihood activities that help households and communities maintain and restore sources of income. Working with national institutions and local organizations, WFP implements activities including climate-resilient agriculture, greenhouses, vegetable farms, sheep and poultry production, and technical and vocational training for youth and people with disabilities. In Gaza, WFP also supports cash-for-work activities and works with retailers, traders and communities as they recover livelihoods and rebuild local economic activity where conditions allow.</div>
                  <aside class="accordion__item-side">
                          <div class="accordion__item-image">
                <img src="https://www.wfp.org/sites/default/files/styles/page_accordion/public/images/Palestine-livelihood-support-WFP-Ali-Jadallah.jpeg?itok=JDpF-Fmc" alt="For Noora tomatoes are red gold. In the photo, Noora is in her greenhouse, arranging her freshly picked tomatoes in boxes to use at home or send to family and friends. Photo: WFP/Ali Jadallah">
              </div>
                                  </aside>
              </dd>
          <dt class="accordion__item-title" data-js-hook="accordion__item-title" tabindex="0" aria-controls="accordion-panel-3" aria-expanded="false">
        <div>
          <h3>Capacity strengthening</h3>
        </div>
      </dt>
      <dd class="accordion__item-panel" id="accordion-panel-3" aria-hidden="true" inert="">
        <div class="accordion__item-content">WFP works with national institutions to strengthen food security systems and improve the ability to respond to shocks and crises. This includes providing tools, technical expertise and guidance to support food security monitoring and analysis, strengthen the National Social Safety Net, and expand livelihood projects. WFP also supports national partners in protecting food systems and improving the evidence base used for food security decision-making. Through these activities, WFP contributes technical expertise alongside its humanitarian and development programmes.</div>
                  <aside class="accordion__item-side">
                          <div class="accordion__item-image">
                <img src="https://www.wfp.org/sites/default/files/styles/page_accordion/public/images/Palestine-capacity-strenghthening-WFP-Mostafa-Ghroz.jpeg?itok=6ZRxoqm2" alt="WFP supports national institutions with technical expertise and capacity building trainings to boost their ability to respond to natural disasters. Photo:WFP/Mostafa Ghroz">
              </div>
                                  </aside>
              </dd>
          <dt class="accordion__item-title" data-js-hook="accordion__item-title" tabindex="0" aria-controls="accordion-panel-4" aria-expanded="false">
        <div>
          <h3>Enabling partners</h3>
        </div>
      </dt>
      <dd class="accordion__item-panel" id="accordion-panel-4" aria-hidden="true" inert="">
        <div class="accordion__item-content">WFP provides shared services that support the wider humanitarian response in Palestine. Through our cash-based transfer platform, we help humanitarian and development organizations deliver assistance to people in need. WFP also provides logistics coordination and supports an inter-agency community feedback mechanism that allows partners to collect and respond to feedback from affected communities. These systems help humanitarian organizations coordinate assistance and reach people more effectively across Palestine.</div>

                          <div class="accordion__item-image">
                <img src="https://www.wfp.org/sites/default/files/styles/page_accordion/public/images/Palestine-enabling-partners-WFP-Mostafa-Ghroz.jpeg?itok=B5itEX6U" alt="WFP offers its cash-based transfer platform to national institutes and humanitarian institutes to ensure efficient reach to targeted population. Photo: WFP/Mostafa Ghroz">
              </div>
                                  </aside>
              </dd>
      </dl>

Skip to main content
  • About UNRWA
    • Mandate and History
      • Mandate
      • History

      Mandate and History

      UNRWA is the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East. The United Nations General Assembly established UNRWA in 1949 with a mandate to provide humanitarian assistance and protection to registered Palestine Refugees in the Agency’s area of operations pending a just and lasting solution to their plight.

    • Principles and Values
      • Humanitarian Principles
      • Sustainable Development Goals

      Principles and Values

      As an Agency with a humanitarian mandate – to assist and protect Palestine Refugees – humanitarian principles provide the space to make our work possible. From ensuring the sanctity of our shelters in times of crisis, to maintaining access to the most vulnerable populations, to advocating on behalf of Palestine Refugees, the principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, and independence are at the heart of all UNRWA operations.

    • Leadership
      • Our leadership
      • Organisational structure

      Leadership

      UNRWA is led by a Commissioner-General, appointed by the UN Secretary-General. The Commissioner-General is supported by a Deputy Commissioner-General for Programmes and Partnerships and a Deputy Commissioner-General for Operational Support.

    • Funding
      • How we are funded
      • How we spend funds
      • Our partners

      Funding

      UNRWA is funded almost entirely by voluntary contributions, mostly from government donors.

Summary of donation information

🚨 Flooding in Gaza: Families Need Urgent Winter Relief

Heavy rain has flooded tents and damaged essentials belongings across Gaza, leaving displaced families exposed to cold and unsafe conditions.

In some areas, floodwater has mixed with sewage, increasing risk of disease.

UNRWA teams are responding on the ground, clearing floodwater and drainage channels, while continuing to provide cash assistance so families can buy what they need to stay warm and materials to repair damaged shelters to survive.

Donate now to support UNRWA’s emergency response and help families in Gaza.

Frequently Asked Questions

⬇ How will my donation make an impact?

Your support directly supports Palestine Refugees and displaced families in Gaza. Every donation, no matter the amount, helps us reach families with life-saving aid such as water, shelter, healthcare, and more.

⬇ Is my donation tax-deductible?

Donations are tax-deductible in a number of countries:

•    For donors in Canada, contributions are tax-deductible to UNRWA. For more information, click here.
•    For donors in the U.S., contributions to UNRWA USA are tax-deductible.
•    For donors in Spain, contributions to UNRWA Spain are tax-deductible.

For other locations, please consult your tax advisor or contact us at donation@unrwa.org

⬇ Why should I become a monthly donor?

By becoming a monthly donor, you can provide continuous support to refugees in need. Monthly giving ensures we can respond to emergencies immediately and provide sustained support to families in urgent need throughout the year.

⬇ Is my donation Zakat-eligible?

Yes, UNRWA’s Zakat programme is Sharia-compliant, and has been endorsed by leading Islamic institutions, including Al-Azhar, the OIC’s International Islamic Fiqh Academy (IIFA), and Al-Aqsa Mosque. Moreover, the programme follows a 100% Zakat distribution policy, whereby 100% of your Zakat contribution goes directly to Palestine Refugees in need. To dedicate your Zakat to Palestine Refugees in need, click here.

⬇ How can I make a donation via bank transfer?

You can donate via bank transfer to one of our accounts based on your preferred currency. For detailed bank account information, please visit our bank transfer details page. After making your transfer, you can request a receipt by emailing us at donation@unrwa.org with your bank transfer details. Receipts are typically issued within 10 business days.

About Us

Our name, OCHA, stands for the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs. In the occupied Palestinian territory (OPT), as elsewhere around the world, we coordinate emergency response to save lives and protect people in humanitarian crises. We advocate for effective and principled humanitarian action by all, for all.

                    <h1 class="dynamic-content__title-text">International Health Regulations</h1>
            </div>

            <div class="row">
                <div class="col-md-7">
                    <div class="dynamic-content__section-content">
                        
                        <div class="sf_cols tabWidget health-topic_tabWidget tabWrapper" style="display: block;">
                            <div class="sf_colsOut flex-clear" data-placeholder-label="Tab wrapper">
                                <div class="ul-tabs--wrapper">
                                    <ul class="tabs"><li id="tab_1" class="tabs__item active shown" style="width: 33.3333%;"><a href="#tab=tab_1"><span>Overview</span></a></li><li id="tab_2" class="tabs__item shown" style="width: 33.3333%;"><a href="#tab=tab_2"><span>Implementation</span></a></li><li id="tab_3" class="tabs__item shown" style="width: 33.3333%;"><a href="#tab=tab_3"><span>Preparedness</span></a></li><li class="mobile-tab tabs__item hidden" style="width: 33.3333%;"><a href="#tab="><span>More</span></a></li></ul>
                                </div>
                                <div class="sf_colsIn single-tabContent">
        <div class="sf_cols singleTabWrapper visible" data-id="tab_1">
            <div class="sf_colsOut tabHeaderWrapper" data-sf-element="Tab header" data-placeholder-label="Tab header">
                <div class="sf_colsIn tabHeaderText">
                    <div class="sf-content-block content-block">
                        Overview
                    </div>
                </div>
            </div>

            <div class="sf_colsOut tabContent" data-sf-element="Tab contents" data-placeholder-label="Tab contents">
                <div class="sf_colsIn">
                    <p>While disease outbreaks and other acute public health risks and events are often unpredictable and require a range of responses, the International Health Regulations (2005) (IHR) provide an overarching legal framework that defines States Parties’ (countries’) rights and obligations in managing public health risks, events and emergencies that have the potential to cross borders.</p><p>The IHR are an instrument of international law that is legally-binding on 197 countries, including the 194 WHO Member States. They establish rights and obligations for countries, including the requirement to designate or establish Responsible Authorities; establish and maintain core capacities for surveillance and response, as well as at points of entry; notify to WHO public health risks and events with actual or potential international public health implications, regardless of their origin or source; verify information of public health risk and events of which WHO has become aware through informal and unofficial sources.</p><p>The IHR set forth the obligation for WHO to maintain the global public health early warning function and to coordinate international response efforts.</p><p>Additional provisions address the areas of international traffic, such as health documents for international travelers and conveyances on an international voyage. The IHR include important safeguards to protect individual rights in relation to the treatment of personal data, informed consent and non-discrimination in the application of health measures under the Regulations.</p><p> </p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
        <div class="sf_cols singleTabWrapper" data-id="tab_2">
            <div class="sf_colsOut tabHeaderWrapper" data-sf-element="Tab header" data-placeholder-label="Tab header">
                <div class="sf_colsIn tabHeaderText">
                    <div class="sf-content-block content-block">
                        Implementation
                    </div>
                </div>
            </div>

            <div class="sf_colsOut tabContent" data-sf-element="Tab contents" data-placeholder-label="Tab contents">
                <div class="sf_colsIn">
                    <p>The purpose and scope of the International Health Regulations (2005) (IHR) are to prevent, prepare for, protect against, control and provide a public health response to the international spread of disease in ways that are commensurate with and restricted to public health risk and which avoid unnecessary interference with international traffic and trade.</p><p>The responsibility for implementing the IHR rests upon all States Parties, across government sectors, and on WHO.</p><p>The IHR require that all countries have capacity to:</p><ul><li>prevent public health risks and events;</li><li>detect acute public health risks and events in timely matter;</li><li>assess acute public health risks and events guided by Annex 2 of the IHR;</li><li>report public health risks and events to WHO, through the National IHR Focal Points those that may constitute a public health emergency of international concern; and</li><li>respond to public health risks, events, and emergencies.</li></ul><p>The IHR require WHO to:</p><ul><li>maintain the global public health early warning function – through global surveillance and information sharing;</li><li>coordinate international response efforts;</li><li>upon countries’ request, support them in capacity building and response efforts; and</li><li>ensure secretariat-like functions.</li></ul><p> </p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
        <div class="sf_cols singleTabWrapper" data-id="tab_3">
            <div class="sf_colsOut tabHeaderWrapper" data-sf-element="Tab header" data-placeholder-label="Tab header">
                <div class="sf_colsIn tabHeaderText">
                    <div class="sf-content-block content-block">
                        Preparedness
                    </div>
                </div>
            </div>

            <div class="sf_colsOut tabContent" data-sf-element="Tab contents" data-placeholder-label="Tab contents">
                <div class="sf_colsIn">
                    <p dir="ltr">To support countries in strengthening and maintaining their capacities for ensuring rapid detection, verification and response to public health risks, WHO develops and provides tools, guidance and training.</p><p dir="ltr">WHO’s support focuses on the priority needs identified by the WHO Regional and Country Offices, in order to help each country meet its IHR commitment. This includes:</p><ul><li><span style="background-color:transparent;text-align:inherit;text-transform:inherit;white-space:inherit;word-spacing:normal;caret-color:auto;font-size:inherit;font-family:inherit;">designating WHO IHR Contact Points at the headquarters or the regional level;</span></li><li>conducting global public health surveillance and assessment of significant public health events;</li><li>disseminating public health information to Member States; </li><li>offering technical assistance to Member States;</li><li>supporting Member States in their efforts to assess their existing national public health structures and capacities for surveillance and response, including at designated points of entry;</li><li>monitoring the implementation of IHR (2005) and updating guidelines; and</li><li>if required, determining whether or not a particular event constitutes a public health emergency of international concern (PHEIC), with advice from external experts.</li></ul><p>If a PHEIC is declared, WHO develops and recommends the critical health measures for implementation by Member States during such an emergency.</p><p> </p>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>

<section class="component info-text-block    [ mb-40 ml-1/10 mr-1/10 ] [ md:w-14/20 md:mb-50 md:ml-5/20 md:mr-0 ] [ lg:w-13/20 lg:mb-60 ] js-component" id="info-text-block-107296" data-component="info-text-block">
    <div class="container">
        <div class="info-text-block__container [ md:flex md:flex-row md:items-start ] ">
      <div class="info-text-block__intro [ block mb-20 font-tiempos text-16 leading-23 text-red ] [ lg:mb-30 lg:text-22 lg:leading-27 ]">We provide medical and psychological assistance to people affected by the ongoing conflict in the West Bank and Gaza.  </div>      <div class="info-text-block__content">
          <p>In Gaza, the local healthcare system is overstretched, underfunded and deeply impacted by a 16-year blockade. We provide assistance to people affected by burns and trauma with a multi-disciplinary approach, which can include <a data-entity-substitution="canonical" data-entity-type="taxonomy_term" data-entity-uuid="f142bf80-4f2c-48c9-9c9f-a1840d72b236" href="/surgery-trauma-care">surgical care</a>, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, health education, and psychosocial support. <br>
 <br>
In the West Bank, occupation, violence, unemployment and poverty continue to have a profound impact on the <a data-entity-substitution="canonical" data-entity-type="taxonomy_term" data-entity-uuid="9364442a-8275-4705-a41f-9837f1b06027" href="/mental-health">mental health</a> of Palestinians. Our teams offer psychological support in Hebron, Nablus, and Qalqilya. <br>
<br>
We provide healthcare services in H2 area, in Hebron city, where Palestinian residents’ movements are subject to restrictions that severely impede their access to healthcare. We also started running mobile clinics to address the health needs of communities in Masafer Yatta, who are facing home demolitions and an increased risk of forcible transfer.</p>

<div class="expandable-block toolkit [ ml-1/10 mr-1/10 ] [ md:pt-48 md:ml-6/20 ] [ lg:ml-5/20 lg:w-11/20 ] js-expandable-block" id="expandable-block-295549">
    <div class="expandable-block__extended" id="expandable-block-295549-content" aria-hidden="true" style="display: none;"><p><strong>Gaza</strong> <br>In 2025, Israel continued its ruthless campaign in Gaza, not only through brutal and incessant violence, but also through months of blockade, denying people their most basic needs for survival, such as food and water, culminating in famine conditions in some areas in August. By 31 December, 71,266 people had been killed by Israeli forces since the start of the war,* while civilian infrastructure and the health system in the Gaza Strip had been systematically decimated. <br><br>Throughout the year, Palestinians were forcibly displaced and pushed into an ever-shrinking geographic area. MSF teams supporting emergency departments responded to multiple mass-casualty incidents, receiving hundreds of patients killed or injured by Israeli strikes in southern Gaza. We also witnessed how the Israeli authorities increasingly suppressed humanitarian space, including by dismantling the UN-led response and replacing it with a militarised food distribution scheme run by the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation (GHF). This led to violence and <a href="https://www.msf.org/dozens-palestinians-massacred-us-israel-backed-food-distribution-sites">killings at food distribution sites</a>. MSF’s clinics were overwhelmed by patients with gunshot wounds, lacerations, and crush injuries, many of them children, as people were shot at or injured in the chaos as they tried to get food. Across the Strip, our teams treated a growing number of children with moderate and severe malnutrition until the <a href="https://www.msf.org/ceasefire-gaza-humanitarian-aid-must-flow-immediately">ceasefire came into effect on 10 October</a>.  <br><br>MSF called on the Israeli authorities to end the violence, allow humanitarian aid to enter at scale, and dismantle the GHF sites (which stopped functioning after the October ceasefire). Meanwhile, the Israeli authorities introduced a new registration system for international NGOs with restrictive and politicised rules, <a href="https://www.msf.org/msfs-vital-humanitarian-activities-gaza-risk-israeli-registration-rules">fundamentally jeopardising the continuation of humanitarian action</a> in Palestine. <br><br>At the end of August, the Israeli forces launched a large-scale offensive on Gaza City, destroying entire neighbourhoods and forcibly displacing hundreds of thousands of people into the middle of the Strip. As a result, MSF had no option but to relocate teams and <a href="https://www.msf.org/msf-forced-suspend-activities-amid-israeli-offensive-gaza-city">suspend all medical activities in the city at the end of September</a>. <br><br>After a second ceasefire came into effect in October, Palestinians returned to the north, and MSF teams relaunched activities. We returned to public hospitals, resuming paediatric services, burns treatment, and physiotherapy, and helping to repair facilities that were filled with rubble. We also opened multiple medical points to deliver general healthcare in areas where the Israeli forces had destroyed all the health facilities. In spite of the ceasefire, the flow of humanitarian aid into Gaza remained critically inadequate, and Israel continued to block essential items, such as shelter materials and so-called dual use items,** exacerbating the dire winter living conditions. <br><br>In response to the immense needs, we expanded our medical and water and sanitation activities throughout the year. MSF continued to be one of the largest providers of services such as comprehensive care for patients with burns and trauma injuries, which included physiotherapy, dressing wounds, surgery, and maternal and neonatal healthcare. By the end of the year, our teams were supporting six hospitals and seven healthcare centres. We were also running two field hospitals, two clinics, and an inpatient feeding centre, as well as providing clean water to hundreds of thousands of Palestinians in Gaza. <br><br>In 2025, six more MSF colleagues died in Israeli airstrikes or targeted attacks, taking the <a href="https://www.msf.org/remembering-our-colleagues-killed-gaza">total number of MSF staff killed in Gaza</a> to 15. To date, our official request for an independent investigation into these killings has not officially been answered by the Israeli authorities. We have made repeated calls for a sustained and immediate ceasefire, urgent and unhindered access for humanitarian aid, medical evacuations, and an end to the genocide. <br><br><strong>The West Bank</strong> <br>In the West Bank, MSF teams continued to witness the consequences of policies and <a href="https://www.msf.org/msf-teams-see-risk-ethnic-cleansing-west-bank">practices of ethnic cleansing</a>, aimed at forcibly transferring Palestinians from their land and preventing any possibility of return. This included a sharp increase in violence by the Israeli military and settlers, who killed and injured many Palestinians. While not new, we witnessed a clear expansion of Israeli settlements and policies aimed at displacing Palestinians in 2025. The ongoing Israeli Iron Wall military operation, which began in January 2025, forcibly displaced 40,000 people in the northern West Bank within a month, according to UNRWA, the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees.*** Three refugee camps were violently raided and emptied. <a href="https://www.msf.org/west-bank-homes-masafer-yatta-communities-have-been-reduced-rubble">Homes and civilian infrastructure</a> ⁠– including schools and healthcare centres ⁠– were demolished, increasing the likelihood that the displacement will become permanent. MSF operated mobile clinics to deliver general healthcare to thousands of people displaced by the military operations in the north, particularly in Jenin and Tulkarem, and distributed hygiene kits, food parcels, and clean water. <br><br>In Hebron, Nablus, Qalqilya, and Tubas, our operations focused on offering medical and mental health support to people affected by settler attacks, demolitions, and displacement, through both mobile and fixed clinics. The constant fear regarding longer and unpredictable incursions and attacks by both Israeli forces and settlers is taking a significant toll on people’s mental health, increasing feelings of hopelessness and anxiety, as observed by our mental health teams. MSF also conducted training for Palestinian Red Crescent Society volunteers, and supported healthcare facilities with training and donations of supplies, including water and fuel. <br><br><strong>MSF’s registration beyond 2025 </strong><br>Throughout the year, MSF faced severe operational uncertainty, due to Israel’s attempts to control and restrict the activities of humanitarian organisations by demanding they re-register to work in the country and submit private information about Palestinian staff. MSF had considerable and legitimate concerns about sharing this data, and therefore, in August, we provided all information requested, except personal details of our staff, which we refused to provide to the Israeli authorities without guaranteed safeguards. Without registration, which expired on 31 December, MSF is unable to send supplies or international staff into Palestine, but our Palestinian teams remain committed to providing assistance for as long as possible.</p><h5><br><br>*United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA): <a href="https://www.ochaopt.org/content/humanitarian-situation-update-351-gaza-strip" class="ext" data-extlink="" target="_blank" rel="noopener" title="(opens in a new window)">https://www.ochaopt.org/content/humanitarian-situation-update-351-gaza-strip</a><br>**A dual-use item is a product, material, or technology that is intended for legitimate civilian or medical use, but is blocked or restricted from entering the Gaza Strip by Israeli authorities because it could potentially be repurposed for military use. <br>***UNRWA: <a href="https://www.unrwa.org/newsroom/official-statements/large-scale-forced-displacement-west-bank-impacts-40000-people " class="ext" data-extlink="" target="_blank" rel="noopener" title="(opens in a new window)">https://www.unrwa.org/newsroom/official-statements/large-scale-forced-displacement-west-bank-impacts-40000-people </a> <br>     </h5></div>

<section class="component faq [ mb-60 ] [ md:w-14/20 md:ml-5/20 ] [ lg:mb-80 ] js-accordion js-component" id="faq" data-component="faq">
  <div class="container">
    <h2 class="faq__heading [ block mt-0 mb-10 ml-1/10 mr-1/10 font-america text-30 leading-28 ] [ md:mb-30 md:ml-0 md:mr-0 ] [ lg:text-54 lg:leading-48 ]">FAQs</h2>
    <div class="faq__container">
                              
        <div class="faq__item [ border-b border-grey-light ] js-accordion-item">
          <div class="faq__header [ flex items-center relative w-full h-74 pt-20 pb-20 pl-1/10 pr-3/10 ] [ md:pl-0 ] [ lg:h-82 ]">
            <h4 class="faq__title [ m-0 font-tiempos text-12 leading-18 text-black ] [ lg:text-18 lg:leading-23 ]" id="faq-title-1">Where does MSF’s money come from?</h4>
            <button type="button" class="faq__toggle [ block absolute pin-t pin-r mt-20 mr-1/10 w-24 h-24 bg-red rounded-full ] [ md:w-28 md:h-28 md:mt-22 md:mr-0 ] [ lg:w-32 lg:h-32 lg:mt-25 ] js-accordion-title" data-target="faq-collapse-1" data-expand-label="Expand Where does MSF’s money come from?" data-collapse-label="Collapse Where does MSF’s money come from?" aria-label="Expand Where does MSF’s money come from?" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="faq-collapse-1">
                <span class="icon icon-add icon--white [ absolute pin m-auto ]">
      <svg aria-hidden="true" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 14 14" style="enable-background:new 0 0 14 14;" xml:space="preserve">

</svg>
    </span>
                <span class="icon icon-remove icon--white [ hidden absolute pin m-auto ]">
      <svg aria-hidden="true" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 14 2" style="enable-background:new 0 0 14 2;" xml:space="preserve">

          </div><!-- /.faq__header -->
          <div class="faq__content [ block pl-1/10 pr-1/10 ] js-accordion-content" id="faq-collapse-1" aria-labelledby="faq-title-1" aria-hidden="true">
            <div class="faq__body [ pb-30 ] [ md:pb-40 ] js-accordion-body"><p>We pride ourselves on the incredible support of our donors. Our funding structure relies on lots of donations from millions of individuals around the world. It is our donors, who fuel MSF’s work.</p><p>In 2025, 98 per cent of our income came from some 7.5 million private donors. It is thanks to the generosity of these private supporters – mainly individuals like you, but also companies and private foundations – that we are able to operate independently and provide humanitarian assistance in some of the world’s most insecure environments and forgotten crises.</p><p>The remaining two per cent of our income came from public institutions, other sales and financial transactions.</p><p>For more details, see the <a href="https://www.msf.org/reports-and-finances#ifr">International Financial Report</a>. </p></div>
          </div>
        </div><!-- /.faq__item -->                        
        <div class="faq__item [ border-b border-grey-light ] js-accordion-item">

            <h4 class="faq__title [ m-0 font-tiempos text-12 leading-18 text-black ] [ lg:text-18 lg:leading-23 ]" id="faq-title-2">How much money does MSF raise every year?</h4>

                <span class="icon icon-add icon--white [ absolute pin m-auto ]">
      <svg aria-hidden="true" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 14 14" style="enable-background:new 0 0 14 14;" xml:space="preserve">

</svg>
    </span>
                <span class="icon icon-remove icon--white [ hidden absolute pin m-auto ]">
      <svg aria-hidden="true" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 14 2" style="enable-background:new 0 0 14 2;" xml:space="preserve">

    </span>
            </button>
          </div><!-- /.faq__header -->
          <div class="faq__content [ block pl-1/10 pr-1/10 ] js-accordion-content" id="faq-collapse-2" aria-labelledby="faq-title-2" aria-hidden="true">
            <div class="faq__body [ pb-30 ] [ md:pb-40 ] js-accordion-body"><p>In 2025, we raised a total of €2.6 billion: 98 per cent of that came from private donations.</p><p>For more details, see the <a href="https://www.msf.org/reports-and-finances#ifr">International Financial Report.</a></p></div>
          </div>
        </div><!-- /.faq__item -->                        
        <div class="faq__item [ border-b border-grey-light ] js-accordion-item">
          <div class="faq__header [ flex items-center relative w-full h-74 pt-20 pb-20 pl-1/10 pr-3/10 ] [ md:pl-0 ] [ lg:h-82 ]">
            <h4 class="faq__title [ m-0 font-tiempos text-12 leading-18 text-black ] [ lg:text-18 lg:leading-23 ]" id="faq-title-3">How is the money spent?</h4>
            <button type="button" class="faq__toggle [ block absolute pin-t pin-r mt-20 mr-1/10 w-24 h-24 bg-red rounded-full ] [ md:w-28 md:h-28 md:mt-22 md:mr-0 ] [ lg:w-32 lg:h-32 lg:mt-25 ] js-accordion-title" data-target="faq-collapse-3" data-expand-label="Expand How is the money spent?" data-collapse-label="Collapse How is the money spent?" aria-label="Expand How is the money spent?" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="faq-collapse-3">
                <span class="icon icon-add icon--white [ absolute pin m-auto ]">
      <svg aria-hidden="true" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 14 14" style="enable-background:new 0 0 14 14;" xml:space="preserve">
  <path d="M14,8H8v6H6V8H0V6h6V0h2v6h6V8z"></path>
</svg>
    </span>
                <span class="icon icon-remove icon--white [ hidden absolute pin m-auto ]">
      <svg aria-hidden="true" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 14 2" style="enable-background:new 0 0 14 2;" xml:space="preserve">
  <path d="M14,2H0V0h14V2z"></path>
</svg>
    </span>
            </button>
          </div><!-- /.faq__header -->
          <div class="faq__content [ block pl-1/10 pr-1/10 ] js-accordion-content" id="faq-collapse-3" aria-labelledby="faq-title-3" aria-hidden="true">
            <div class="faq__body [ pb-30 ] [ md:pb-40 ] js-accordion-body"><p>Your donations pay for millions of consultations, surgeries, treatments and vaccinations every year.</p><p>We are a non-profit organisation and 79% of our financial resources are allocated to fulfilling our social mission: 63% to our humanitarian programmes, 13% to support our projects and programmes, and 3% to our bearing witness (témoignage) activities. The rest is spent on general management and fundraising costs. We also maintain reserves that allow us to respond immediately to a crisis without having to wait for an appeal. The use of MSF funds is tightly controlled and the audited financial reports are publicly available.</p><p>The overwhelming majority of our programmes are implemented directly by our teams. In other cases, we provide support to local medical networks who can directly access those in need. This is notably notably the case in Syria where some areas of the country are not directly accessible to our teams.</p><p>For a more detailed breakdown of our sources of income, by activity and by geographic area, see the <a href="https://www.msf.org/reports-and-finances#ifr">International Financial Report.</a></p></div>
          </div>

            <h4 class="faq__title [ m-0 font-tiempos text-12 leading-18 text-black ] [ lg:text-18 lg:leading-23 ]" id="faq-title-4">Where is the money spent?</h4>
            <button type="button" class="faq__toggle [ block absolute pin-t pin-r mt-20 mr-1/10 w-24 h-24 bg-red rounded-full ] [ md:w-28 md:h-28 md:mt-22 md:mr-0 ] [ lg:w-32 lg:h-32 lg:mt-25 ] js-accordion-title" data-target="faq-collapse-4" data-expand-label="Expand Where is the money spent?" data-collapse-label="Collapse Where is the money spent?" aria-label="Expand Where is the money spent?" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="faq-collapse-4">

          <div class="faq__content [ block pl-1/10 pr-1/10 ] js-accordion-content" id="faq-collapse-4" aria-labelledby="faq-title-4" aria-hidden="true">
            <div class="faq__body [ pb-30 ] [ md:pb-40 ] js-accordion-body"><p>In 2025, 60% of programme expenditure was spent in Africa, 10% was spent in Asia, and the rest in Europe, the Americas, Oceania and for transversal activities, such as search and rescue.<br><br>We spent the most in Democratic Republic of Congo, Sudan, Palestine, South Sudan, Nigeria, Yemen, Chad, Central African Republic, Afghanistan, and Niger.</p><p>The <a href="https://www.msf.org/reports-and-finances#ifr">International Financial Report</a> gives more details of the geographic distribution of expenditure. It also provides breakdowns of expenses and funding for all the countries where MSF has significant programme activities in a given year.</p></div>
          </div>
        </div><!-- /.faq__item -->

          <div class="faq__header [ flex items-center relative w-full h-74 pt-20 pb-20 pl-1/10 pr-3/10 ] [ md:pl-0 ] [ lg:h-82 ]">
            <h4 class="faq__title [ m-0 font-tiempos text-12 leading-18 text-black ] [ lg:text-18 lg:leading-23 ]" id="faq-title-5">Does MSF restrict donations from companies?</h4>
            <button type="button" class="faq__toggle [ block absolute pin-t pin-r mt-20 mr-1/10 w-24 h-24 bg-red rounded-full ] [ md:w-28 md:h-28 md:mt-22 md:mr-0 ] [ lg:w-32 lg:h-32 lg:mt-25 ] js-accordion-title" data-target="faq-collapse-5" data-expand-label="Expand Does MSF restrict donations from companies?" data-collapse-label="Collapse Does MSF restrict donations from companies?" aria-label="Expand Does MSF restrict donations from companies?" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="faq-collapse-5">
                <span class="icon icon-add icon--white [ absolute pin m-auto ]">
      <svg aria-hidden="true" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 14 14" style="enable-background:new 0 0 14 14;" xml:space="preserve">
  <path d="M14,8H8v6H6V8H0V6h6V0h2v6h6V8z"></path>
</svg>
    </span>
                <span class="icon icon-remove icon--white [ hidden absolute pin m-auto ]">
      <svg aria-hidden="true" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 14 2" style="enable-background:new 0 0 14 2;" xml:space="preserve">

    </span>

          </div><!-- /.faq__header -->
          <div class="faq__content [ block pl-1/10 pr-1/10 ] js-accordion-content" id="faq-collapse-5" aria-labelledby="faq-title-5" aria-hidden="true">
            <div class="faq__body [ pb-30 ] [ md:pb-40 ] js-accordion-body"><p>We don't accept contributions from companies and industries whose core activities may be in direct conflict with, or limit our ability to provide, medical humanitarian work. Hence, we don't accept money from pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, extraction industries (such as oil, natural gas, gold, or diamonds), tobacco companies and arms manufacturers.</p><p>Additional limitations may exist in the national giving acceptance policies of the countries where MSF is fundraising.</p></div>

            <h4 class="faq__title [ m-0 font-tiempos text-12 leading-18 text-black ] [ lg:text-18 lg:leading-23 ]" id="faq-title-6">Does MSF accept donations of medical products?</h4>
            <button type="button" class="faq__toggle [ block absolute pin-t pin-r mt-20 mr-1/10 w-24 h-24 bg-red rounded-full ] [ md:w-28 md:h-28 md:mt-22 md:mr-0 ] [ lg:w-32 lg:h-32 lg:mt-25 ] js-accordion-title" data-target="faq-collapse-6" data-expand-label="Expand Does MSF accept donations of medical products?" data-collapse-label="Collapse Does MSF accept donations of medical products?" aria-label="Expand Does MSF accept donations of medical products?" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="faq-collapse-6">
                <span class="icon icon-add icon--white [ absolute pin m-auto ]">
      <svg aria-hidden="true" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 14 14" style="enable-background:new 0 0 14 14;" xml:space="preserve">
  <path d="M14,8H8v6H6V8H0V6h6V0h2v6h6V8z"></path>
</svg>
    </span>
                <span class="icon icon-remove icon--white [ hidden absolute pin m-auto ]">
      <svg aria-hidden="true" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 14 2" style="enable-background:new 0 0 14 2;" xml:space="preserve">
  <path d="M14,2H0V0h14V2z"></path>
</svg>
    </span>
            </button>
          </div><!-- /.faq__header -->
          <div class="faq__content [ block pl-1/10 pr-1/10 ] js-accordion-content" id="faq-collapse-6" aria-labelledby="faq-title-6" aria-hidden="true">
            <div class="faq__body [ pb-30 ] [ md:pb-40 ] js-accordion-body"><p>MSF does not accept in-kind donations of medical products or health technology. Only under exceptional circumstances, and on a case-by-case basis, MSF may consider accepting such donations according to the criteria and conditions set forth in <a href="https://www.msf.org/sites/msf.org/files/msf-policy-in-kind-donations-medical-products-health-technology-2018.pdf">MSF’s Policy for In-Kind Donations of Medical Products and Health Technology (PDF)</a>.</p></div>
          </div>
        </div><!-- /.faq__item -->                        
        <div class="faq__item [ border-b border-grey-light ] js-accordion-item">
          <div class="faq__header [ flex items-center relative w-full h-74 pt-20 pb-20 pl-1/10 pr-3/10 ] [ md:pl-0 ] [ lg:h-82 ]">
            <h4 class="faq__title [ m-0 font-tiempos text-12 leading-18 text-black ] [ lg:text-18 lg:leading-23 ]" id="faq-title-7">Can I choose where my money goes?</h4>
            <button type="button" class="faq__toggle [ block absolute pin-t pin-r mt-20 mr-1/10 w-24 h-24 bg-red rounded-full ] [ md:w-28 md:h-28 md:mt-22 md:mr-0 ] [ lg:w-32 lg:h-32 lg:mt-25 ] js-accordion-title" data-target="faq-collapse-7" data-expand-label="Expand Can I choose where my money goes?" data-collapse-label="Collapse Can I choose where my money goes?" aria-label="Expand Can I choose where my money goes?" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="faq-collapse-7">
                <span class="icon icon-add icon--white [ absolute pin m-auto ]">
      <svg aria-hidden="true" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 14 14" style="enable-background:new 0 0 14 14;" xml:space="preserve">
  <path d="M14,8H8v6H6V8H0V6h6V0h2v6h6V8z"></path>
</svg>
    </span>
                <span class="icon icon-remove icon--white [ hidden absolute pin m-auto ]">
      <svg aria-hidden="true" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 14 2" style="enable-background:new 0 0 14 2;" xml:space="preserve">
  <path d="M14,2H0V0h14V2z"></path>
</svg>
    </span>
            </button>
          </div><!-- /.faq__header -->
          <div class="faq__content [ block pl-1/10 pr-1/10 ] js-accordion-content" id="faq-collapse-7" aria-labelledby="faq-title-7" aria-hidden="true">
            <div class="faq__body [ pb-30 ] [ md:pb-40 ] js-accordion-body"><p>We appreciate that some of our supporters may have a particular interest in a country or programme in which we work. While in some circumstances it is possible to have your gift directed toward a specific programme or country, we ask that you contribute with unrestricted funding.</p><p>Unrestricted general donations give us the ability to direct funds where the needs are greatest, including under-reported and neglected crises.</p><p>MSF would not be able to swiftly respond to emergencies in Central African Republic, South Sudan or Yemen, nor provide lifesaving care to hundreds of thousands of people living with HIV, if not for the general support from our donors worldwide.</p></div>
          </div>
        </div><!-- /.faq__item -->                        
        <div class="faq__item [ border-b border-grey-light ] js-accordion-item">
          <div class="faq__header [ flex items-center relative w-full h-74 pt-20 pb-20 pl-1/10 pr-3/10 ] [ md:pl-0 ] [ lg:h-82 ]">

</svg>
    </span>

</svg>
    </span>
            </button>
          </div><!-- /.faq__header -->
          <div class="faq__content [ block pl-1/10 pr-1/10 ] js-accordion-content" id="faq-collapse-8" aria-labelledby="faq-title-8" aria-hidden="true">
            <div class="faq__body [ pb-30 ] [ md:pb-40 ] js-accordion-body"><p>Further details on where our money comes from, how much we raise, and how we spend it, can be found in our <a href="/reports-and-finances#ifr">International Financial Report</a>.</p><p>The International Financial Report also gives details on where we spend your money, showing the geographic distribution of our expenditure, and providing breakdowns of expenses and funding for all the countries where MSF has significant programme activities in a given year.</p></div>

<section class="component faq [ mb-60 ] [ md:w-14/20 md:ml-5/20 ] [ lg:mb-80 ] js-accordion js-component" id="warning" data-component="faq">
  <div class="container">
    <h2 class="faq__heading [ block mt-0 mb-10 ml-1/10 mr-1/10 font-america text-30 leading-28 ] [ md:mb-30 md:ml-0 md:mr-0 ] [ lg:text-54 lg:leading-48 ]">Warning</h2>
    <div class="faq__container">
                              
        <div class="faq__item [ border-b border-grey-light ] js-accordion-item">
          <div class="faq__header [ flex items-center relative w-full h-74 pt-20 pb-20 pl-1/10 pr-3/10 ] [ md:pl-0 ] [ lg:h-82 ]">
            <h4 class="faq__title [ m-0 font-tiempos text-12 leading-18 text-black ] [ lg:text-18 lg:leading-23 ]" id="warning-title-1">Scams, hoaxes and frauds involving MSF</h4>
            <button type="button" class="faq__toggle [ block absolute pin-t pin-r mt-20 mr-1/10 w-24 h-24 bg-red rounded-full ] [ md:w-28 md:h-28 md:mt-22 md:mr-0 ] [ lg:w-32 lg:h-32 lg:mt-25 ] js-accordion-title" data-target="warning-collapse-1" data-expand-label="Expand Scams, hoaxes and frauds involving MSF" data-collapse-label="Collapse Scams, hoaxes and frauds involving MSF" aria-label="Expand Scams, hoaxes and frauds involving MSF" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="warning-collapse-1">
                <span class="icon icon-add icon--white [ absolute pin m-auto ]">
      <svg aria-hidden="true" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 14 14" style="enable-background:new 0 0 14 14;" xml:space="preserve">
  <path d="M14,8H8v6H6V8H0V6h6V0h2v6h6V8z"></path>
</svg>
    </span>
                <span class="icon icon-remove icon--white [ hidden absolute pin m-auto ]">
      <svg aria-hidden="true" role="img" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 14 2" style="enable-background:new 0 0 14 2;" xml:space="preserve">
  <path d="M14,2H0V0h14V2z"></path>
</svg>
    </span>
            </button>
          </div><!-- /.faq__header -->
          <div class="faq__content [ block pl-1/10 pr-1/10 ] js-accordion-content" id="warning-collapse-1" aria-labelledby="warning-title-1" aria-hidden="true">
            <div class="faq__body [ pb-30 ] [ md:pb-40 ] js-accordion-body"><p>Please be aware there have been cases of individuals posing as Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) staff in order to scam people out of money.</p>

<p>MSF has received reports of third parties attempting to fraudulently obtain money on our behalf via email, social networking websites or apps, or in person at public locations.</p>

<p>The following is a list of scams and hoaxes that have been brought to our attention (please note this list is not exhaustive):</p>

<ul>
	<li>An individual or individuals carrying out what appears to be fraudulent collections of money in public locations, while pretending to represent MSF.<br>
	 </li>
	<li>People posing as MSF staff in emails asking for reimbursements for donations, sometimes naming actual MSF staff or senior management in their appeals in order to bring a sense of credibility.<br>
	 </li>
	<li>People posing as MSF staff requesting money to pay for individual medical procedures for fictitious patients.<br>
	 </li>
	<li>People posing as MSF staff who have been detained on their way home and asking for money to be transferred in order to secure their release from detention. <br>
	 </li>
	<li>People posing as MSF staff, or acting on behalf of MSF staff, on social networking websites or apps in order to lure unsuspecting members of the public to send funds to cover the travel costs of the alleged MSF staff member to return from a field mission.<br>
	 </li>
	<li>​People posing as MSF staff who have been detained on their way home and asking for money to be transferred in order to secure their release from detention. <br>
	 </li>
	<li>People posing as MSF human resources or recruitment staff asking people applying for a job with MSF for money or to pay a fee.</li>
</ul>

<p>All MSF staff are instructed to call their home MSF office if they find themselves in an unfortunate situation like losing their passport or if they have trouble with a visa. We then provide all the support they need to get home.</p>

<p>MSF staff in the field will also have access to funds in an emergency situation and so have no need to request financial support from anyone, for either themselves or their patients.<br>
<br>
MSF does not charge a fee at any stage of the recruitment process (application, interview meeting, processing, training or any other fees).</p>

<p>Unfortunately there is nothing we can do to stop scams such as these and others from happening. If you are unsure if you are the subject of a scam or fraud involving a supposed MSF staff member, <a href="/contact-us">please get in contact with your local or nearest MSF office</a>. You can also get in touch with your country’s local consumer commission or fraud reporting office.</p>
</div>

<section class="fc-intro-section">

    <div class="column small-12 medium-7">
      <h3>Gaza’s 2.1 million civilians are facing a major humanitarian crisis. Violence across the Gaza Strip has displaced more than 90% of the population, leaving them with limited access to healthcare, food, water and other essential services.</h3>
<p><span class="s1">International Medical Corps has provided lifesaving humanitarian assistance and protection services in Gaza since 2008, focusing on emergency preparedness, coordination and delivery of primary and secondary healthcare, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), child protection (CP), nutrition, and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services, as well as services to address violence against women and girls (VAWG).</span></p>
<p>International Medical Corps has provided lifesaving humanitarian assistance and protection services in Gaza since 2008, focusing on emergency preparedness, coordination and delivery of primary and secondary healthcare, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), child protection (CP), nutrition, and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services, as well as services to address violence against women and girls (VAWG).</p>
<p>We have deployed fully equipped field hospitals, and work with international and local partners to implement vaccination and malnutrition campaigns to help children throughout Gaza.</p>

<section class="fc-list_content-block ">

  
      <div class="fc-section-title">
      <h2>Our Response</h2>
    </div>
  

            <div class="list-content-item">
        <div class="row">
          <div class="column small-3 medium-2">

            <div class="img-container no-background">
                              <img src="https://cdn1.internationalmedicalcorps.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Country-Response_Survivor-Care.svg">
                          </div>


          </div>
          <div class="column small-9 medium-10">
                        <p>The ever-changing security situation and ongoing tensions compound the challenges of humanitarian response in Gaza. Before the conflict escalated in 2023, our work focused on implementing emergency preparedness and coordination projects, and on providing primary and secondary healthcare, MHPSS, CP, and services to address VAWG.</p>
<p>Following the conflict’s escalation, we adapted our services to meet the dire humanitarian needs of Gazan civilians, including establishing large, fully functional field hospitals to provide civilians with surgical and trauma services, outpatient services, MHPSS, CP, nutrition and WASH services.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>



          <div class="list-content-item">
        <div class="row">
          <div class="column small-3 medium-2">

            <div class="img-container no-background">
                              <img src="https://cdn1.internationalmedicalcorps.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Country-Response_Emergency-Response-Preparedness-1.svg">
                          </div>


          </div>
          <div class="column small-9 medium-10">
                        <h3>Primary and Secondary Healthcare</h3>
                        <p>Our field hospitals and multi-purpose centers together provide comprehensive primary healthcare services—including outpatient consultations, disease prevention and treatment, routine immunizations, and maternal and newborn healthcare—to displaced populations across Gaza. The hospitals are classified as Level 4 primary healthcare centers.</p>
<p>Our hospital in central Gaza focuses primarily on internal medicine and on comprehensive maternal and newborn health services. It has an emergency room, an operating theater and a neonatal intensive-care unit (NICU), supported by a laboratory, a pharmacy, a blood bank and a radiology department.</p>
<p>Our field hospitals in the north provide comprehensive medical services focused on trauma care, patient rehabilitation, surgeries and maternity care, offering operating rooms, an intensive care unit and a NICU. The hospitals also offer physiotherapy, integrated protection and nutrition services.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>



          <div class="list-content-item">
        <div class="row">
          <div class="column small-3 medium-2">

            <div class="img-container no-background">
                              <img src="https://cdn1.internationalmedicalcorps.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Country-Response_Nutrition-2.svg">
                          </div>


          </div>
          <div class="column small-9 medium-10">
                        <h3>Nutrition</h3>
                        <p>We provide integrated nutrition services through 10 sites at the community and facility levels. These services include malnutrition screening, outpatient therapeutic programs, targeted supplementary-feeding programs, blanket supplementary-feeding programs, infant and young-child feeding (IYCF) programs and a stabilization center.</p>
<p>Regular screening enables early identification and treatment of acute malnutrition. We provide clinical nutrition support to pediatric and adult inpatients through assessments, therapeutic nutrition plans, counseling and monitoring. Our IYCF programming includes counseling, support groups, cooking demonstrations and mother-baby spaces that promote safe infant-feeding practices. We also provide therapeutic and ready-to-eat meals to inpatients.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>



          <div class="list-content-item">
        <div class="row">
          <div class="column small-3 medium-2">

            <div class="img-container no-background">
                              <img src="https://cdn1.internationalmedicalcorps.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Country-Response_Water-Sanitation-Hygiene-1.svg">
                          </div>


          </div>
          <div class="column small-9 medium-10">
                        <h3>Water, Sanitation and Hygiene</h3>
                        <p>Our technical experts lead the design, construction and maintenance of critical WASH infrastructure, including reliable water-supply systems with desalination and backup units; accessible sanitation facilities, such as toilets, showers and handwashing stations; and comprehensive waste-management systems that cover medical and general waste through segregation and safe disposal, following strict infection-prevention and control standards.</p>
<p>We raise awareness of handwashing, safe-waste storage and waterborne-disease prevention through hygiene-promotion activities. During emergencies, we deliver safe water to displaced communities through multiple distribution points—ensuring safe, dignified and continuous care in challenging environments.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>



          <div class="list-content-item">
        <div class="row">
          <div class="column small-3 medium-2">

            <div class="img-container no-background">
                              <img src="https://cdn1.internationalmedicalcorps.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Country-Response_Mental-Health-Psychosocial-Support.svg">
                          </div>


          </div>
          <div class="column small-9 medium-10">
                        <h3>Mental Health and Psychosocial Support</h3>
                        <p>Our MHPSS work strengthens social connections and promotes positive coping strategies through comprehensive, multi-tiered MHPSS services aligned with the Inter-Agency Standing Committee (IASC) pyramid and the World Health Organization’s Mental Health Gap Action Programme. We provide MHPSS services through a multidisciplinary team of psychiatrists, psychologists and psychosocial workers who support those experiencing distress, as well as mental, neurological and substance-use conditions.</p>
<p>We use tools such as Self-Help Plus as well as peer-support activities in group sessions to strengthen coping skills and build social connections. In our hospitals and through outreach, our community prevention and promotion activities include psychoeducation, stigma reduction, healing ceremonies and awareness sessions. We help local healthcare workers, volunteers and partner organizations integrate MHPSS into existing systems.</p>
<p>We have established the first inpatient center for mental health—called the Acute Psychiatric Stabilization Unit—in central Gaza to provide specialized psychiatric care and mental health services to people experiencing psychological distress.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>



          <div class="list-content-item">
        <div class="row">
          <div class="column small-3 medium-2">

            <div class="img-container no-background">
                              <img src="https://cdn1.internationalmedicalcorps.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/Country-Challenges_Children’s-Health-3.svg">
                          </div>


          </div>
          <div class="column small-9 medium-10">
                        <h3>Child Protection</h3>
                        <p>Since establishing our field hospitals, we have expanded our CP interventions to include structured and unstructured psychosocial activities in our child-friendly space. The CP team provides case management, counseling, psychological first aid (PFA), and parenting and awareness sessions to build resilience and strengthen coping.</p>
<p>Children in inpatient care receive daily psychosocial support, including during medical procedures. Our team also supports unaccompanied and separated children by providing structured case management. Our comprehensive approach helps to reduce CP risks and ensure a safe, supportive environment that upholds children’s rights and dignity.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

                          </div>


          </div>
          <div class="column small-9 medium-10">
                        <h3>Violence Against Women and Girls</h3>
                        <p>Recognizing the needs of women and girls at risk of violence in conflict-affected settings, we provide information sessions, PFA, individual support sessions and targeted interventions to educate the community on how to recognize, prevent and report VAWG. We connect survivors to medical care and psychosocial support through specialized case management.</p>
<p>To provide holistic assistance, we integrate all protection services with medical care. Our teams coordinate referrals internally and externally, and provide protection training for our staff and partners.</p>
<p>To further support women and girls, we operate women’s and girls’ safe spaces (WGSSs) that offer safe environments for information-sharing, social support and skills training. Our WGSS activities build resilience, promote well-being and reduce the risk of VAWG through survivor-centered programming.</p>

			<script>
				// Used by Gallery Custom Links to handle tenacious Lightboxes.
				//
				// 2026/08/15: Until now this walked the DOM on load and set onclick = null on
				// the images. That only ever removed handlers assigned as an onclick *property*,
				// so every lightbox binding through addEventListener survived it: jQuery ones,
				// delegated ones, and WordPress core's own "Expand on click" (the Interactivity
				// API binds data-wp-on--click on the img, and its showLightbox() calls neither
				// preventDefault nor stopPropagation). The lightbox opened and the link was
				// followed at the same time, or the lightbox swallowed the click entirely.
				//
				// One listener on window in the capture phase fixes all of them at once: capture
				// runs from the top of the tree down, so we see the click before anything bound
				// on the image itself and can stop it from ever getting there. We deliberately do
				// NOT preventDefault, which leaves the browser to follow the link on its own, so
				// target, ctrl/cmd-click and middle-click all keep behaving natively. Being
				// delegated, it also covers galleries added to the page after load (AJAX,
				// infinite scroll), which the old load-time pass never saw.
				window.addEventListener('click', function (ev) {
					if (!ev.target || !ev.target.closest) {
						return;
					}
					if (!ev.target.closest('a.no-lightbox, a.set-target')) {
						return;
					}
					ev.stopPropagation();
					if (ev.stopImmediatePropagation) {
						ev.stopImmediatePropagation();
					}
				}, true);

          <h1 class="entry-title">

			<script>
				// Used by Gallery Custom Links to handle tenacious Lightboxes.
				//
				// 2026/08/15: Until now this walked the DOM on load and set onclick = null on
				// the images. That only ever removed handlers assigned as an onclick *property*,
				// so every lightbox binding through addEventListener survived it: jQuery ones,
				// delegated ones, and WordPress core's own "Expand on click" (the Interactivity
				// API binds data-wp-on--click on the img, and its showLightbox() calls neither
				// preventDefault nor stopPropagation). The lightbox opened and the link was
				// followed at the same time, or the lightbox swallowed the click entirely.
				//
				// One listener on window in the capture phase fixes all of them at once: capture
				// runs from the top of the tree down, so we see the click before anything bound
				// on the image itself and can stop it from ever getting there. We deliberately do
				// NOT preventDefault, which leaves the browser to follow the link on its own, so
				// target, ctrl/cmd-click and middle-click all keep behaving natively. Being
				// delegated, it also covers galleries added to the page after load (AJAX,
				// infinite scroll), which the old load-time pass never saw.
				window.addEventListener('click', function (ev) {
					if (!ev.target || !ev.target.closest) {
						return;
					}
					if (!ev.target.closest('a.no-lightbox, a.set-target')) {
						return;
					}
					ev.stopPropagation();
					if (ev.stopImmediatePropagation) {
						ev.stopImmediatePropagation();
					}
				}, true);

<div class="prose prose-md text-foreground-strong font-bold pt-scale-md max-w-content"><p data-block-key="fwpcb">People with disabilities in Gaza, the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and refugee camps in Lebanon face immense barriers to basic services. Violence, discrimination, displacement and poverty have stripped away access to healthcare, assistive devices, rehabilitation and safe, accessible spaces. Movement restrictions, destroyed infrastructure and overcrowded living conditions make daily life even harder.</p></div>

    <div class="container max-w-wrapper grid-centered-8 richtext [&+.heading-3]:-mt-scale-2xs">
        <div class="prose max-w-content">
            <p data-block-key="43xot">Since October 2023, the crisis in Gaza has deepened and the challenges have grown. Bombed hospitals, disrupted services, and inaccessible shelters have left many people with disabilities cut off from vital care and support. The physical and emotional toll is growing, and there is an urgent need for inclusive, rights-based, tailored support that enables them to reclaim their dignity and independence.</p>
        </div>

<div class="container max-w-wrapper grid-centered-8 heading-2 [&+.richtext]:-mt-scale-2xs">
    <h2 class="heading-2 max-w-content" id="going-beyond-inclusion">Going beyond inclusion</h2>
</div>


    


    <div class="container max-w-wrapper grid-centered-8 richtext [&+.heading-3]:-mt-scale-2xs">
        <div class="prose max-w-content">
            <p data-block-key="l7fvv">We’re working towards a future where people with disabilities are not just included, but given the support they need to thrive.</p><ul><li data-block-key="3ud1m">Disability support is built into everything we do: we work to remove physical, social and systemic barriers to ensure inclusion across all our programmes.</li><li data-block-key="du6f4">Community-led rehabilitation: our targeted rehab services and local outreach help people with disabilities access care close to home, regain independence and build resilience.</li><li data-block-key="6me7d">Challenge and change: we support people with disabilities to challenge stigma, shift public perceptions and become active leaders in their communities.</li><li data-block-key="dh320">Nothing about us without us: people with disabilities help shape our projects from the beginning, ensuring their needs and voices are at the heart of every decision.</li><li data-block-key="88ab8">Long-term impact: by strengthening individuals, families and health systems, we create lasting, dignified solutions - available even in times of crisis.</li></ul>
        </div>
    </div>

NRC in Palestine

Displaced Palestinians make their way back to their homes in northern Gaza. Photo: Amjad Al Fayoumi/NRC
Gaza continues to endure an ongoing humanitarian catastrophe. During two years of hostilities, the majority of the population was displaced and tens of thousands of Palestinians killed.
Updated 22. Sep 2026
Palestine

Despite a ceasefire agreement reached in October 2025, the situation remains critical, with frequent Israeli strikes, severe supply shortages and restrictions blocking humanitarian access and assistance.

In addition to Gaza, the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, is facing a displacement and protection crisis. Israeli military operations, government-backed settler violence, demolitions, forced evictions and settlement expansion continue to uproot Palestinian families and further destabilise the region. Despite the challenges, the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is continuing with its efforts to save lives, protect rights and ease suffering.  

What’s happening in Palestine?

In October 2023, attacks by Palestinian armed groups resulted in the deaths of approximately 1,200 Israelis and foreign nationals, with over 250 people taken hostage. In response, Israel launched devastating strikes on Gaza, leaving entire communities in ruins. Widespread destruction of homes and infrastructure displaced at least 1.9 million people – around 90 per cent of Gaza’s population. Many families, including the small percentage who were able to return, remain without safe shelter or access to basic services. 

The ongoing siege and restrictions on humanitarian access have resulted in critical shortages of food, clean water, shelter and medical supplies that put countless lives at risk. Although a ceasefire agreement was reached in October 2025, severe humanitarian access constraints remain, and the risk of renewed hostilities continues. 

The West Bank, including East Jerusalem, is facing its largest and most prolonged displacement crisis since 1967. Violence continues to rise, with Israeli settler attacks increasing in frequency and intensity alongside expanding settlement activity, land appropriation and forced displacement. Intensified Israeli military operations in the northern West Bank displaced tens of thousands of Palestinians from refugee camps, leaving many people in an increasingly vulnerable situation. 

Across the occupied Palestinian territory, bureaucratic restrictions, logistical barriers and the closure of crossings and checkpoints continue to delay or block life-saving assistance.  

Urgent international action is needed to prevent further loss of life, ensure safe humanitarian access and uphold the rights of Palestinians. 

Our response

We’re working with our partners in Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, in the following areas:

  • Water, sanitation and hygiene – expanding access to safe drinking water, sanitation facilities and hygiene supplies, while supporting waste management and emergency water distribution. 
  • Shelter and site management – supporting displaced families with emergency shelter, essential household items, shelter repairs, and working to strengthen the safety, dignity and environment of displacement sites. 
  • Education – providing learning opportunities and psychosocial support to children and youth who have experienced trauma and interruptions to their education through the establishment of safe learning spaces and developing the capacity of facilitators, teachers and counsellors. 
  • Protection from violence – supporting individuals and communities to prevent and respond to violence, reduce protection risks and strengthen safety, dignity and resilience. 
  • Information, counselling and legal assistance – supporting people in safeguarding their housing, land and property rights, helping to protect people from demolition, eviction and confiscation orders, as well as access restrictions, residency revocation and discrimination.

    (function() {
      function getCookie(cname) {
        let name = cname + "=";
        let decodedCookie = decodeURIComponent(document.cookie);
        let ca = decodedCookie.split(';');
        for (let i = 0; i < ca.length; i++) {
          let c = ca[i];
          while (c.charAt(0) == ' ') {
            c = c.substring(1);
          }
          if (c.indexOf(name) == 0) {
            return c.substring(name.length, c.length);
          }
        }
        return "";
      }

      if (getCookie('campaignsuite-nightmode') == 'true') {
        document.documentElement.setAttribute('prefers-color-scheme', 'dark');
      } else {
        document.documentElement.setAttribute('prefers-color-scheme', 'light');
      }

      if (getCookie('campaignsuite-rtl') == 'true') {
        document.documentElement.setAttribute('dir', 'rtl');
      } else {
        document.documentElement.setAttribute('dir', 'ltr');
      }

      if (getCookie('campaignsuite-listview') == 'true') {
        document.documentElement.setAttribute('listview', 'list');
      } else {
        document.documentElement.setAttribute('listview', 'grid');
      }
    })();
  </script>

<h2 id="gspb_heading-id-gsbp-7c73fe3" class="gspb_heading gspb_heading-id-gsbp-7c73fe3 ">The world’s most neglected displacement crises</h2>



<p id="gspb_text-id-gsbp-8981dae" class="gspb_text gspb_text-id-gsbp-8981dae ">Nearly 118 million people are displaced by war and conflict. While a few crises capture the world’s attention, millions of children, families, and older people are suffering in total silence, cut off from the aid they need.</p>

<div class="wp-block-greenshift-blocks-accordionitem gs-accordion-item gspb_accordionitem-gsbp-4d4cb21 gsclose" id="gspb_accordionitem-gsbp-4d4cb21" itemscope="" itemprop="mainEntity" itemtype="https://schema.org/Question"><div id="gs-trigger-gsbp-e762505-0" class="gs-accordion-item__title" aria-expanded="false" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-controls="gspb-accordion-item-content-gsbp-4d4cb21"><h3 class="gs-accordion-item__heading">What happens to your donation?</h3><meta itemprop="name" content="What happens to your donation?"><span class="iconfortoggle"><span class="gs-iconbefore"></span><span class="gs-iconafter"></span></span></div><div aria-labelledby="gs-trigger-gsbp-e762505-0" class="gs-accordion-item__content" itemscope="" itemprop="acceptedAnswer" itemtype="https://schema.org/Answer" id="gspb-accordion-item-content-gsbp-4d4cb21"><div class="gs-accordion-item__text" itemprop="text">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Your donation supports our work for people forced to flee, providing emergency assistance, shelter, education, legal assistance and protection to children and families affected by war and conflict. <br><br>More than 90% of our income goes directly to our work for people forced to flee.</p>
</div></div></div>



<div class="wp-block-greenshift-blocks-accordionitem gs-accordion-item gspb_accordionitem-gsbp-71f2907 gsclose" id="gspb_accordionitem-gsbp-71f2907" itemscope="" itemprop="mainEntity" itemtype="https://schema.org/Question"><div id="gs-trigger-gsbp-e762505-1" class="gs-accordion-item__title" aria-expanded="false" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-controls="gspb-accordion-item-content-gsbp-71f2907"><h3 class="gs-accordion-item__heading">About NRC</h3><meta itemprop="name" content="About NRC"><span class="iconfortoggle"><span class="gs-iconbefore"></span><span class="gs-iconafter"></span></span></div><div aria-labelledby="gs-trigger-gsbp-e762505-1" class="gs-accordion-item__content" itemscope="" itemprop="acceptedAnswer" itemtype="https://schema.org/Answer" id="gspb-accordion-item-content-gsbp-71f2907"><div class="gs-accordion-item__text" itemprop="text">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">We provide emergency assistance and protect people’s rights in the world’s most challenging crises. Our scale and expertise mean we can reach and assist millions in areas where others cannot.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Your support allows us to react quickly in crises and help those who need it most. We provide housing, education, protection from violence, and other critical services.</p>
</div></div></div>



<div class="wp-block-greenshift-blocks-accordionitem gs-accordion-item gspb_accordionitem-gsbp-dbbecb4 gsclose" id="gspb_accordionitem-gsbp-dbbecb4" itemscope="" itemprop="mainEntity" itemtype="https://schema.org/Question"><div id="gs-trigger-gsbp-e762505-2" class="gs-accordion-item__title" aria-expanded="false" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-controls="gspb-accordion-item-content-gsbp-dbbecb4"><h3 class="gs-accordion-item__heading">Contact us</h3><meta itemprop="name" content="Contact us"><span class="iconfortoggle"><span class="gs-iconbefore"></span><span class="gs-iconafter"></span></span></div><div aria-labelledby="gs-trigger-gsbp-e762505-2" class="gs-accordion-item__content" itemscope="" itemprop="acceptedAnswer" itemtype="https://schema.org/Answer" id="gspb-accordion-item-content-gsbp-dbbecb4"><div class="gs-accordion-item__text" itemprop="text">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Email:</strong> <a href="mailto:fundraising@nrc.no" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">fundraising@nrc.no</a></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Phone:</strong> +47 800 33 503 Mon–Fri, 10:00–12:00 and 12:30–14:00 CEST.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>SMS:</strong> +47 594 48 256</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Address: </strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Prinsens gate 2<br>0152 Oslo<br>Norway</p>
</div></div></div>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Please contact <a href="mailto:corporate@nrc.no">corporate@nrc.no</a> if you have any questions!</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Bank transfer:</strong><br>Use the information below to make a donation by bank transfer.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">IBAN #: NO59 8210 0465 007<br>SWIFT code: DNBANOKKXXX</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Norwegians can use account number 8200.06.80008 and mark the payment “Corporate gift”.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Benevity:</strong><br>If you are a user of the Benevity workplace giving platform, you can donate to our cause by searching for “Norwegian Refugee Council” while logged in to your Benevity account.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Global Giving:</strong><br>If you are a user of the Global Giving platform, you can donate to our cause <a href="https://www.globalgiving.org/projects/helping-people-forced-to-flee/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">here</a>.</p>
