<div class="block-type--paragraph_components view-mode--full block block-layout-builder block-inline-blockparagraph-components clearfix contextual-region">
  
      <h2 class="h2 section-title red-label">Save the Children in the Occupied Palestinian Territory</h2>
    
        

<div class="text paragraph-separator">
  
            <div class="text-long"><p class="text-align-justify"><span>Save the Children has worked in the occupied Palestinian territory (oPt) since 1953, with a permanent presence since 1973. Since then, we have worked with partners to help provide quality education, protection for children, early childhood development support, and employment opportunities for at-risk youth. We also focus on child-centred climate change programming, advocacy and campaigning, on environmental education, community-based adaptation and climate activism.</span></p><p class="text-align-justify"><span>Operating in severe insecurity amid unprecedented levels of violence, systematic obstruction of aid by Israeli authorities, famine and the near collapse of all formal services in Gaza, as well as hostilities, continued displacement and increased settler violence in the West Bank, we have rapidly adapted our programming to remain operational and responsive. Despite the increasingly complex and evolving situation, we are doing all we can to ensure we reach children and their families. </span></p></div>
      
</div>


  </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="layout layout--onecol">
    <div class="layout__region layout__region--content">
      

<div class="block-type--paragraph_components view-mode--full block block-layout-builder block-inline-blockparagraph-components clearfix contextual-region">
  
      <h2 class="h2 section-title red-label">The situation for children in Occupied Palestinian Territory</h2>
    
        

<div class="text paragraph-separator">
  
            <div class="text-long"><p class=""><strong>Palestinian children continue to carry the weight of the occupation. </strong>Decades of conflict, the ongoing military occupation, and the blockade of Gaza hinder the right to self-determination and consequently have adverse impacts on the development of Palestinian communities, greatly increasing the vulnerability of children.</p><p class=""><strong>For too long, the occupation has denied the rights of Palestinian children and stolen their childhoods, exposing them to violence, arbitrary detentions, and cutting them off from their homes, schools and other essential services. </strong>Ultimately, the root causes of repeated bouts of violence and a decades-long child rights crisis in the oPt must be addressed. Only an end to the occupation can create the conditions for lasting peace and protection for children.</p><p class="">Palestinian children are the only children in the world who are systematically prosecuted in military courts. These courts consistently fail to offer the right to a fair trial and do not meet juvenile justice standards. Instead, it is an abusive, inhumane prosecution system, where children are being physically, emotionally and sexually abused, humiliated and starved.  </p><p class=""><strong>The widespread and systematic ill-treatment of Palestinian children within the Israeli military system is a long-standing human rights and child rights crisis.</strong> All Palestinian children arbitrarily held in Israeli military detention must be released immediately and unconditionally. No child should ever come in contact with a military court or any court that lacks comprehensive fair trial rights and basic safeguards. This decades-old protection crisis for Palestinian children has reached devastating new levels of abuse and deprivation. </p></div>
      
</div>


  </div>

<div class="block-type--paragraph_components view-mode--full block block-layout-builder block-inline-blockparagraph-components clearfix contextual-region">

  <div class="caption_text">
    <p>Nour*, 4, lost all her family in an Israeli bombing that targeted the entire block where her family lived during the early days of the war in Gaza. The bombing blew her from her family’s apartment, at a height of 30 meters, to the street, and she broke her two legs, among other injuries, on top of her pre-existing hearing and speech disability.  Shurouq Alaila/ Save the Children</p>
  </div>

<div class="block-type--paragraph_components view-mode--full block block-layout-builder block-inline-blockparagraph-components clearfix contextual-region">
  
    
          

<div class="has-grey-background text text--with-bg paragraph-separator">
  
            <div class="text-long"><h3 class="">GAZA</h3><p class="" style="line-height:normal;margin-bottom:12.0pt;"><strong>Tens of thousands of children have been killed by bombs and bullets. More have lost their homes and loved ones.</strong> The harm children are facing will have long-term and potentially irreversible impacts, undermining their futures and the future of Palestinian society as a whole. T<strong>he ceasefire agreement remains fragile and has shown very little respite for children and families. </strong>The implementation of the ceasefire plan <a href="https://resourcecentre.savethechildren.net/document/humanitarian-scorecard-six-months-in-gaza-ceasefire-is-failing">is failing</a>. </p><p class="" style="line-height:normal;margin-bottom:12.0pt;"><strong>The blocking of aid and goods from entering Gaza by Israeli authorities is continuing to have catastrophic impacts on children. </strong>Through the deregistration of international NGOs and existing barriers, Israeli authorities are undermining the delivery of lifesaving humanitarian assistance to children and families in oPt at a moment of unprecedented need.  </p><p class="" style="line-height:normal;margin-bottom:12.0pt;">Students and teachers <a href="https://www.savethechildren.net/stories/education-occupied-palestinian-territory-under-attack">across the oPt</a> have been killed, maimed, arrested, and detained. In Gaza, we’re at risk of seeing a “lost” generation emerge. Children are now in their third year of missing school and need to get back to the classroom, not only for their own individual development and futures but for the future of Palestinian society.  </p></div>
      
</div>


  </div>

<div class="block-type--paragraph_components view-mode--full block block-layout-builder block-inline-blockparagraph-components clearfix contextual-region">
  
    
          

<div class="has-grey-background text text--with-bg paragraph-separator">
  
            <div class="text-long"><h3 class="">THE WEST BANK</h3><p class="" style="line-height:normal;margin-bottom:4.0pt;">Every day, Palestinian children and their families are confronted with the daily violence of a military occupation.<strong> Children are forced to grow up in an asphyxiating, coercive environment</strong> marked by state-sanctioned violence, racial discrimination, the loss of loved ones, detention, and the destruction of homes and schools. These practices are strangulating the aspirations and futures of Palestinian children and devastating their mental health. </p><p class="" style="line-height:normal;margin-bottom:4.0pt;"> </p><p class="" style="line-height:normal;margin-bottom:4.0pt;">Children can't safely access education either; <strong>over 621,000 children are attending school only three times a week.</strong> Children and teachers are telling our teams they are being harassed, detained and attacked on their way to and during school, while increased checkpoints, road closures, and access impediments are severely disrupting children's access to learning.</p><p class="" style="line-height:normal;margin-bottom:4.0pt;"> </p><p class="" style="line-height:normal;margin-bottom:4.0pt;">The siege-like tactics on communities in the West Bank are fraying the very fabric of Palestinian life and society, by separating Palestinian communities and families from each other, children from their schools and parents from their places of employment, creating conditions for Palestinians incompatible with life. Israeli forces and settlers are dismantling and obstructing vital humanitarian aid. <strong>Israeli authorities’ policies and practices are resulting in the annexation of the West Bank and violating the territorial integrity of the oPt and Palestinians’ right to self-determination.</strong>  </p></div>
      
</div>


  </div>

  <div class="caption_text">
    <p>Homes, schools, health facilities and infrastructure have been completely destroyed in Khan Younis in the Gaza Strip.

The war on Gaza since the 7 October attacks on Israel by Palestinian armed groups has resulted in horrendous consequences for children. More than 13,800 children in Gaza have been killed, as well as 106 children in the West Bank and 33 children in Israel. 

The humanitarian situation in Gaza is dire. Homes, hospitals and schools have been destroyed. More than 1.7 million people have been displaced. Now, more than one million children face the imminent threat of famine. 

Amidst extremely challenging conditions, Save the Children staff and partners have been working around the clock to support the most vulnerable children and families. Sacha Myers / Save the Children</p>

  <div class="caption_text">
    <p>Fatima*, 40, is a mother of three.
her children are a 13-year-old girl (not pictured), 16-year-old Sami* and 19-year-old Maysa*. They are displaced and received a food parcel from Save the Children, distributed by partner organisation Beir Lahia Development Association.

A distribution of food parcels was carried out for families living in a camp in Deir Al-Balah.
The food parcels included cheese, fava beans, hummus, beans, olives, tuna, fruit jam, tahini, tea, sugar, halva, dates, za’atar, olive oil, canned meat, peas, some disposable plates and containers, as well as wet wipes.

  <div class="caption_text">
    <p>Radwa*, 30, is a mother of five from Gaza whose children face severe medical challenges worsened by the ongoing war. Her youngest daughter Basma*, 1, suffered from malnutrition after Radwa* struggled to breastfeed following major surgery and due to lack of food because of the war and siege on Gaza since 2 March. 

Save the Children provided vital support through breastfeeding support sessions, helping Radwa* continue breastfeeding Basma* and care for her children. Save the Children has also provided Ready to Use Therapeutic Food (peanut paste) for Basma* to help her recover from malnutrition. Although we were able to help Basma* this time, supplies of Ready to Use Therapeutic Food are now running out in the Gaza Strip.
 
Radwa's* eldest daughter, Mais*, 11, has a lung tumour, her son Karam*, 7, has autism and seizures.
 
Despite daily hardships and a lack of food and medical care, Radwa* remains grateful for the support that has been crucial to her children’s survival and well-being. Eyad AlTawil / Save the Children</p>

<div class="text paragraph-separator">
  
            <div class="text-long"><h3 class=" h3__secondary--bold">Save the Children is the world's leading organisation for children.             <div class="text-long"><h3>WHY WORK FOR SAVE THE CHILDREN?</h3><p>The work here is challenging, but is also immensely rewarding. At Save the Children, you will be in good company, working with talented, like-minded individuals who are determined to ensure that all children survive, learn, and are protected.</p><h3>WHAT ARE WE LOOKING FOR?</h3><p>We look for candidates who share our passion and dedication to making a real difference in the world. You'll need to demonstrate a commitment to our mission and values, as well as our child safeguarding policy.</p><p>Each role will have its own requirements, but broadly speaking we look for candidates who have a high-level of technical competence, and are able to work collaboratively in a highly-matrixed, and culturally-diverse organisation. We need people who can deliver to a high standard, in often challenging circumstances, both ethically and professionally.</p><p>For some roles, you will need to be able to travel internationally, and may need to be internationally mobile to develop your career. Any requirement for international travel will be outlined in the job description.</p></div>

      <h2 class="h2 section-title red-label">FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS</h2>
    
      

      <div>
                          <div class="first-item accordion-item">



  
  


<dl class="accordion">
  <dt class="accordion__title">
      
  
  
  
<h4 class="h4">
         I am interested in working for Save the Children, but I don’t see a suitable vacancy advertised. How can I set up an email alert for suitable vacancies?
  </h4>
  </dt>
  <dd class="accordion__content">
        <p>Please visit our <a href="https://hcri.fa.em2.oraclecloud.com/hcmUI/CandidateExperience/en/sites/CX_1/join-talent-community">careers portal</a> to set up an account and profile. Once your profile is set up, click on the 'My Jobs' page, and then 'Access my profile'. Under the 'Preferences tab', you can create email alerts for new vacancies by the business function and location.</p>
    </dd>
</dl></div>
                        <div class="accordion-item">



  
  


<dl class="accordion">
  <dt class="accordion__title">
      
  
  
  
<h4 class="h4">
        I’m interested in a role in one of your country offices, but don’t see it on the careers portal. Where can I find the posting and apply? 
  </h4>
  </dt>
  <dd class="accordion__content">
        <p>Roles available in our country offices for national staff will not be listed on this careers portal at this time. Please visit our <a href="/about-us/contact-us">country websites</a> for those vacancies.</p>
    </dd>
</dl></div>
                        <div class="accordion-item">



  
  


<dl class="accordion">
  <dt class="accordion__title">
      
  
  
  
<h4 class="h4">
        I’m interested in a role in one of your member offices, but don’t see it on the careers portal. Where can I find the posting and apply?
  </h4>
  </dt>
  <dd class="accordion__content">
        <p>All roles available in our member offices will not be listed on this career portal until 2020. Please visit our <a href="/where-we-work">member websites</a> for those vacancies in the meantime.</p>
    </dd>
</dl></div>
                        <div class="accordion-item">



  
  


<dl class="accordion">
  <dt class="accordion__title">
      
  
  
  
<h4 class="h4">
        I am interested in applying for a role where I do not currently have the right to work. Does Save the Children support with visas and work permits?
  </h4>
  </dt>
  <dd class="accordion__content">
        <p>Where a candidate is required to have the existing right to work in that country, it will be listed as an essential requirement. Otherwise, there is the potential for Save the Children to support with a visa or work permit.</p>
    </dd>
</dl></div>
                        <div class="accordion-item">



  
  


<dl class="accordion">
  <dt class="accordion__title">
      
  
  
  
<h4 class="h4">
        I am interested in applying for a vacancy but would like to confirm the salary before applying?
  </h4>
  </dt>
  <dd class="accordion__content">
        <p>We invite all candidates to confirm their salary expectations on application, if you are shortlisted for interview this will be discussed with you at this time.</p>
    </dd>
</dl></div>
                        <div class="accordion-item">



  
  


<dl class="accordion">
  <dt class="accordion__title">
      
  
  
  
<h4 class="h4">
        I am applying from a country which the US applies sanctions to, and I get an error message when I try to submit an online application via ReliefWeb and LinkedIn. How can I submit my application?
  </h4>
  </dt>
  <dd class="accordion__content">
        <p>Please apply directly via the relevant Save the Children website and your application will be received.</p>
    </dd>
</dl></div>
                        <div class="accordion-item">



  
  


<dl class="accordion">
  <dt class="accordion__title">
      
  
  
  
<h4 class="h4">
        Can I make any changes to my application once it has been submitted?
  </h4>
  </dt>
  <dd class="accordion__content">
        <p>You can make changes to your application by logging into your account on the <a href="https://hcri.fa.em2.oraclecloud.com/hcmUI/CandidateExperience/en/sites/CX_1/join-talent-community">careers portal</a>.</p>
    </dd>
</dl></div>
                        <div class="accordion-item">



  
  


<dl class="accordion">
  <dt class="accordion__title">
      
  
  
  
<h4 class="h4">
        How long will it take to hear back on my application?
  </h4>
  </dt>
  <dd class="accordion__content">
        <p>We will be in touch within four weeks of the closing date to confirm if we have short-listed your application.</p>
    </dd>
</dl></div>
                        <div class="accordion-item">



  
  


<dl class="accordion">
  <dt class="accordion__title">
      
  
  
  
<h4 class="h4">
        I would like to volunteer for Save the Children. How do I learn about available opportunities? 
  </h4>
  </dt>
  <dd class="accordion__content">
        <p>All volunteer opportunities are advertised on our website. We do not accept speculative applications.</p>
    </dd>
</dl></div>
                        <div class="accordion-item">



  
  


<dl class="accordion">
  <dt class="accordion__title">
      
  
  
  
<h4 class="h4">
        Does Save the Children offer internships? How do I register my interest?
  </h4>
  </dt>
  <dd class="accordion__content">
        <p>Save the Children offers paid internships in our London office. These vacancies are advertised on our website.</p>
    </dd>
</dl></div>
                        <div class="accordion-item">



  
  


<dl class="accordion">
  <dt class="accordion__title">
      
  
  
  
<h4 class="h4">
        Does Save the Children offer work placement opportunities? 
  </h4>
  </dt>
  <dd class="accordion__content">
        <p>We do not offer work placements on a formal basis, but in some instances arrangements can be made through schools or universities. Please note that we do not accept individual requests.</p>
    </dd>
</dl></div>
                        <div class="accordion-item">



  
  


<dl class="accordion">
  <dt class="accordion__title">
      
  
  
  
<h4 class="h4">
        I am locked out of my account on your e-recruitment system. How do I reset my password?
  </h4>
  </dt>
  <dd class="accordion__content">
        <p>Please request a new password on the e-recruitment system by selecting 'Forgot your password'. If you're still having problems, please contact <a href="mailto:scirecruitment@savethechildren.org">scirecruitment@savethechildren.org</a> for assistance.</p>
    </dd>
</dl></div>

      <div>
                          <div class="first-item accordion-item">



  
  


<dl class="accordion">
  <dt class="accordion__title">
      
  
  
  
<h4 class="h4">
        Our Reward Approach
  </h4>
  </dt>
  <dd class="accordion__content">
        <p>People are at the heart of Save the Children and this is the fundamental principle in our reward approach, which is designed to help us attract, retain, develop and mobilise the best talent. Our Reward approach supports and reflects Save the Children's mission, strategy, and values, as well as our commitment to fairness and diversity.</p><p>Many talented and passionate people join Save the Children to make a difference, and monetary reward will not be the primary motivator. Our reward offer ensures a minimum standard of living for our employees and their families, as well as a fair and proportionate reward for the contribution our employees make to delivering positive change for children. We provide:</p><ul><li>Family-friendly policies including flexible working, maternity/parental leave</li><li>Competitive pay (as per the INGO market) which takes into account relevant skills, competencies and experiences</li><li>A competitive benefits package, as per the sector and relevant local market</li><li>Support for international relocations (where applicable)</li></ul>
    </dd>
</dl></div>
                        <div class="accordion-item">



  
  


<dl class="accordion">
  <dt class="accordion__title">
      
  
  
  
<h4 class="h4">
        Supporting Your Learning and Development
  </h4>
  </dt>
  <dd class="accordion__content">
        <p>At Save the Children, we are committed to supporting your development and helping you to enhance the impact you have on the organisation. We offer a varied curriculum of management and leadership development, personal effectiveness, technical and specialist practitioner training, which blends formal development with on the job learning. Where possible, we also support our staff to achieve externally recognised professional qualifications, and to take up opportunities to participate in working groups across our sector; which help you to build your network and enable us to benefit from industry learning and best practice.</p>
    </dd>
</dl></div>
                        <div class="accordion-item">



  
  


<dl class="accordion">
  <dt class="accordion__title">
      
  
  
  
<h4 class="h4">
        Developing Capable and Diverse Leaders
  </h4>
  </dt>
  <dd class="accordion__content">
        <p>We are focused on developing capable and diverse leaders who will enable the delivery of our global strategy. We offer a varied, best in class and bespoke leadership development curriculum, which reflects the demands and challenges of leading in a complex, global organisation. We invest in the development of our talented leaders and allow them to shape their own learning curriculum to reflect the needs and challenges of their individual roles. This includes targeted leadership coaching and intentional moves to different parts of our organisation in addition to formal learning.</p>
    </dd>
</dl></div>
                        <div class="accordion-item">



  
  


<dl class="accordion">
  <dt class="accordion__title">
      
  
  
  
<h4 class="h4">
        Why Work for Save the Children?           
  </h4>
  </dt>
  <dd class="accordion__content">
        <p>The work here is challenging, but is also immensely rewarding. At Save the Children, you will be in good company, working with talented, like-minded individuals who are determined to ensure that all children survive, learn, and are protected.</p>
    </dd>
</dl></div>
                        <div class="accordion-item">



  
  


<dl class="accordion">
  <dt class="accordion__title">
      
  
  
  
<h4 class="h4">
        What Are We Looking For?
  </h4>
  </dt>
  <dd class="accordion__content">
        <p>We look for candidates who share our passion and dedication to making a real difference in the world. You'll need to demonstrate a commitment to our mission and values, as well as our child safeguarding policy.<br>Each role will have its own requirements, but broadly speaking we look for candidates who have a high-level of technical competence, and are able to work collaboratively in a highly-matrixed, and culturally-diverse organisation. We need people who can deliver to a high standard, in often challenging circumstances, both ethically and professionally.</p><p>For some roles, you will need to be able to travel internationally, and may need to be internationally mobile to develop your career. Any requirement for international travel will be outlined in the job description.</p>
    </dd>
</dl></div>

      <div><p><span lang="EN-US">Oxfam has been working in the occupied Palestinian territory (oPt) since the 1950s, establishing a country office in the 1980s. Together with partner organisations we work with the most vulnerable communities in Gaza and the West Bank. Our joint efforts focus on improving livelihoods and advancing the rights of communities living under illegal occupation, prolonged suffering, deprivation and hardship.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Oxfam has been delivering life‑saving humanitarian aid and programmatic support to communities across the oPt for decades. We work to facilitate humanitarian access and the delivery of assistance in line with international humanitarian law. Oxfam, together with partner organisations, responds to the humanitarian crisis with programming in areas including vital water infrastructure and other repair and maintenance work; hygiene kit distribution; livelihoods and agricultural support; food security interventions, and water sanitation and hygiene (WASH) activities. Our work also focuses on responding to needs around the protection of civilians, psycho-social support, and the rights of women.</span></p></div>

      <div><p><span lang="EN-US">Informed by partners and programmes, and founded on principles of International Humanitarian Law (IHL) and International Human Rights Law, Oxfam advocates for accountability and an immediate end to the decades-long cycle of violence in the oPt as a result of the ongoing impunity afforded to Israel, which has fueled further human rights violations, war crimes and other violations of international law.</span><br><span lang="EN-US"></span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">The international community has failed to ensure the equal rights and self-determination of the Palestinian people as guaranteed in the UN Charter Article 1(2).       <div><h2><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Impacts of Israel’s illegal occupation in the oPt </strong></span><br><span lang="EN-US"></span></h2><p><span lang="EN-US">In Gaza, the combined effects of Israel's illegal occupation of the oPt (including severe restrictions on the flow of vital aid and goods, and denial of freedom of movement) continue to deepen an already severe humanitarian catastrophe. Water scarcity is escalating, with some areas of Gaza City receiving as little as two litres of drinking water per person per day.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">The overwhelming majority of Palestinians in Gaza continue to live in makeshift shelters or heavily damaged structures, facing severe shortages of food, drinking water, medical supplies, fuel, shelter materials, WASH items and cooking gas.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">From October 2023 to </span><a href="https://www.unrwa.org/resources/reports/unrwa-situation-report-225-humanitarian-crisis-gaza-strip-and-occupied-west-bank"><span lang="EN-US">June 2026,</span></a><span lang="EN-US"> amidst Israel’s ongoing genocide on Gaza, over 72,000 Palestinians were killed, and more than 173,000 injured. </span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Almost the entire population of Gaza - 2.1 million people - has been displaced, lacking access to sufficient shelter, food, life-saving medical services, clean water, education and livelihoods. In the West Bank, more than 30,000 Palestinian people have been forcibly displaced. </span></p><p><span lang="EN-GB">At the same time, the destruction of civilian infrastructure has been catastrophic: </span><a href="https://www.ochaopt.org/content/reported-impact-snapshot-gaza-strip-6-may-2026"><span lang="EN-GB">92 % of assessed commercia</span></a><span lang="EN-GB">l and industrial establishments have been destroyed or damaged. </span><a href="https://www.ochaopt.org/content/reported-impact-snapshot-gaza-strip-6-may-2026"><span lang="EN-GB">74% of the road network</span></a><span lang="EN-GB"> has been destroyed, as well as </span><a href="https://www.ochaopt.org/content/reported-impact-snapshot-gaza-strip-6-may-2026"><span lang="EN-GB">90% of energy infrastructure</span></a><span lang="EN-GB"> – including the electricity distribution network and associated assets. </span><a href="https://www.ohchr.org/en/press-releases/2024/06/states-and-companies-must-end-arms-transfers-israel-immediately-or-risk"><span lang="EN-GB">UN experts</span></a><span lang="EN-GB"> and </span><a href="https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2025/09/global-political-economy-enabling-israels-genocide-occupation-apartheid/"><span lang="EN-GB">human rights organizations</span></a><span lang="EN-GB"> have warned that companies supplying weapons or military support to Israel may risk complicity in serious violations of human rights.</span><span lang="EN-US"></span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">In the West Bank, severe access constraints, closures and movement restrictions continue to intensify. New checkpoints and gate closures have further fragmented communities, limiting mobility for residents and humanitarian staff, yet despite the enormous challenges, Oxfam and partners continue to advance the response, sustaining coordination and scaling support where possible.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">A surge in settler violence and intensified movement restrictions is further impacting on Palestinian communities. More Palestinians have been killed by the Israeli military and settlers across the occupied West Bank in the last three years than in the previous 17 years combined.</span></p></div>
  
</div>

      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--text paragraph--view-mode--default max-width-text mx-auto content-section-text copy-body">
  
      <div><h2><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Oxfam position on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict</strong></span><span lang="EN-US"></span></h2><p><span lang="EN-US"></span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Civilians must be protected under international law, A sustainable and just peace for Palestinians and Israelis requires ending the military occupation, addressing root causes of the conflict, and ensuring accountability for all parties. Gaza requires an immediate full and permanent ceasefire, unimpeded humanitarian access, and urgent rehabilitation of basic services.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US"></span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">A permanent ceasefire in Gaza is imperative to help stop further loss of life, deliver required levels of humanitarian aid, avoid the total destruction of civic infrastructure like schools and hospitals, and cultural history. Without a permanent ceasefire, it is simply impossible for the international humanitarian system to work safely to distribute aid and help protect the lives of civilians.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US"></span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">The international community must advocate towards a long-term political solution beyond humanitarian relief. This should include the dismantling of Illegal settlements, cessation of their expansion in oPt and an end to Israel's illegal military occupation, the lifting of Israeli blockade and restrictions that hamper the Palestinian economy and the movement of people and goods, and support for Palestinian self-determination and access to international forums and legal mechanisms.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US"></span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">International efforts are needed now more than ever to facilitate a peace process that will lead to a viable, permanent status agreement ensuring equality, security, dignity, sovereignty, justice and prosperity, both for Palestinians and Israelis.</span></p><h2><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Oxfam’s registration in Israel</strong></span><span lang="EN-US"></span></h2><p><span lang="EN-US"></span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Following the introduction of new procedures for INGO registration and the recent Israeli High Court ruling dismissing an appeal challenging these procedures from 18 humanitarian organisations including Oxfam, Oxfam is no longer registered in Israel and annexed East Jerusalem.  We continue our operations and work with our local partners in the oPt on the basis of our registration with the Palestinian Authority. </span></p></div>
  
</div>

    <h2 class="text-orange w-full">Right to live without a blockade</h2>
        <div class="w-full"><p><strong>The impact of Israeli access and movement restrictions on the Gaza economy</strong></p><p> </p><p>Beginning in the early 1990s, the Israeli government introduced incremental measures to restrict the movement of people and goods between Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, as well as cutting off Gaza from the rest of the world.</p><p> </p></div>

      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--text paragraph--view-mode--default max-width-text mx-auto content-section-text copy-body">
  
      <div><p><span lang="EN-US">Every year since 2008, the world has become less peaceful. From climate-related disasters to long-lasting conflicts and insecurity, we witnessed a rise in the scale and frequency of humanitarian crises, increasing the number of vulnerable people, displaced, at risk or in need of assistance.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">In Syria, Yemen, or South Sudan, conflicts continue to threaten and destroy the lives of millions of women, men and children, trapping them in a vicious cycle of violence, poverty and inequality. Hunger is again on the rise, reversing years of progress.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">The number of climate-related disasters has tripled in 30 years, causing harm and suffering to communities across the globe. By the 2030s, large parts of Southern, Eastern and the Horn of Africa, and South and East Asia will experience greater exposure to droughts, floods, and tropical storms.</span></p></div>
  
</div>
      </div>
      </div>

          
  <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--text paragraph--view-mode--default">
          <div class="bg-beige-light border-burgundy border-l-8 clear-both max-width-text mx-auto p-6">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--text paragraph--view-mode--default max-width-text mx-auto content-section-text copy-body">
  
      <div><h2><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Let's look at the numbers</strong></span></h2><p class="highlight">Overall, more than <strong>132 million</strong> people across the world need humanitarian assistance and protection.</p><p class="highlight"><strong>One-third</strong> of the world’s poor live in fragile and conflict-affected countries. By 2030, this share is likely to grow to one-half.</p><p class="highlight"><span lang="EN-US">In 2019 the number of people who have been forced from their homes by war and persecution reached <strong>68 million</strong> –  the highest number since World War II.</span></p><p class="highlight"><span lang="EN-US">The number of people going hungry worldwide is growing, reaching <strong>690 million</strong> in 2019.</span></p><p class="highlight"><span lang="EN-US">An Oxfam’s analysis shows that, on average, <strong>14 million</strong> people were reported newly displaced by extreme weather disasters each year over the period 2008-2016.</span></p><style type="text/css">.highlight strong {
font-weight: bold;
font-size: 1.2em;
color: #630235;
}
</style></div>
  
</div>
      </div>
      </div>

          
  <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--text paragraph--view-mode--default">
          <div class="max-width-text mx-auto">
      <div class="paragraph paragraph--type--text paragraph--view-mode--default max-width-text mx-auto content-section-text copy-body">
  
      <div><h2><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Delivering high quality aid: Oxfam's response</strong></span></h2><p><span lang="EN-US">Oxfam has a long and well-recognized record of humanitarian relief in times of crisis. When disaster strikes, we respond - delivering high quality lifesaving assistance and essential protection to the most affected. We make sure people can get clean water to drink and decent sanitation. We provide help for them to get food and the essentials they need to survive, and we work with people on the journey to self-sufficiency.</span></p><p><span lang="EN-US">Through our long-term development programs, we stay well after the dust has settled to help rebuild communities to come back stronger from disaster and support them in being better prepared to cope with shocks and uncertainties.</span></p><h3><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Building resilience and local capacity</strong></span></h3><p><span lang="EN-US">The scale and nature of these humanitarian crises have led us to put more emphasis on building the resilience of affected populations and increasing national and local response capacity and ownership. We recognize that local responders are often the best placed to help in emergencies, and we work with governments, local organizations, and communities so that they are ready to respond in emergencies, and able to cope when crisis hits.</span></p><h3><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Supporting women’s rights and gender justice</strong></span></h3><p><span lang="EN-US">In all our responses, we prioritize the needs of women and girls, who are often discriminated against or have fewer resources to face and recover from emergencies. We promote the safe and accessible use of our humanitarian programs by women and girls, and support women's organizations to lead in emergency preparedness, risk reduction, and response.</span></p><h3><span lang="EN-US"><strong>Campaigning and influencing others</strong></span></h3><p><span lang="EN-US">The goal of our campaigning is not just to speak for people in need, but to open the way for them to speak for themselves. A key part of our humanitarian work is campaigning and using our influence to make sure women, men, and children are provided the assistance they need and have their rights respected. We also seek to address and ultimately remedy the political and structural root causes of their vulnerability. </span></p></div>
  
</div>

  }

  @media (min-width: 871px) and (min-height: 641px) {

      margin-inline-start: calc(100vw - 100vw / 2) !important;
    }

    [dir='rtl'] .swg-dialog,

  @media (min-width: 641px) and (min-height: 641px) {

    }

    }
  }

<h2 id="stories-of-hope-wck-farmers-in-gaza" class="wp-block-heading has-h1-variant">Stories of Hope: WCK Farmers in Gaza</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Across Gaza, the land that once fed communities lies largely dormant. As of May 2025, as much as 95 percent of Gaza’s agricultural land is unusable, and 80 percent of cropland has been damaged or destroyed. Farmers—who for generations have been the backbone of Gaza’s economy and food culture—can no longer access the seeds they need. The result is felt every day in WCK’s kitchens, where fresh produce has become rare, and the meals that do include it carry an outsized meaning for displaced families.</p>

 <div class="text_content">
 <p>HI has been working in the Occupied Palestinian Territory since 1996. Initially, the organisation supported local groups helping people with disabilities. In 1999, it launched a new programme to educate people about the dangers posed by landmines and other unexploded ordnance. Programmes were implemented in partnership with local stakeholders. HI has also responded to successive crises in Palestine and Israel, particularly in the 2000s.  </p>

<p>Following the escalation of the conflict on 7 October 2023, HI has scaled up its emergency response in Gaza. HI's response is structured around four main sectors: Rehabilitation and prosthetics and orthotics, with associated psychosocial support; explosive ordnance risk education and contamination assessment; support for children through recreational activities; inclusive education during emergencies.</p>

<p>Atlas Logistique — the operational logistics unit of HI — runs several logistics platforms to ensure the storage and channelling of humanitarian goods and items for humanitarian organisations operating in Gaza.<br>
In January 2025, HI also opened two prosthetics and orthotics centres in the Gaza Strip to produce and deliver prosthetic limbs for amputees.</p>

<p>In parallel, HI delivers explosive ordnance risk education sessions. The organisation also conducted assessments of contamination by explosive ordnance to support the needed clearance efforts. <br>
Particularly crucial in an environment marked by displacements of population, HI has deployed outreach teams accessing beneficiaries directly within their camps and providing daily rehabilitation sessions and psychosocial support.</p>

<h2 style="font-size: 3em ;color:#0077c8!important;font-weight: lighter ;line-height: 1.1 ;"> Situation of the country </h2>



 <div class="country_situation_header mb-md mt-md">
 <p>The Palestinian people have endured decades of extraordinarily difficult living conditions due to the ongoing conflict between Israel and the Gaza de facto authorities, and the long-standing occupation of the Gaza Strip. Those in the West Bank are also becoming increasingly vulnerable in the face of an increasingly dire socio-economic situation. A lack of employment opportunities, restrictions on the movement of goods and people, and public services that are heavily overstretched and incapable of meeting demand leave many Palestinians struggling to meet their most basic needs. </p>

 </div>
 <div class="country_situation mb-md text_content">
 <p>The 7 October 2023 attacks in Israel, which caused the deaths of around 1,200 people, triggered large-scale airstrikes and ground operations between the Israeli Armed Forces and Palestinian armed factions, which have devastated the Gaza Strip. At least 72,000 Palestinians have been killed and another 172,000 injured in the Gaza Strip. The conflict has also generated a massive disability crisis, with an estimated 5,000 to 6,000 people becoming amputees in the last 2.5 years alone.</p>

<p>The ceasefire agreement, adopted in October 2025, is reportedly being breached on a daily basis. Despite the ceasefire, over 700 Palestinians are reported to have died and countless more have been injured as a result of continued hostilities. Crossings into Gaza are not operating as announced, with only limited supplies permitted to enter the Gaza Strip. This has caused fuel shortages and price increases, resulting in greater reliance on humanitarian assistance. For instance, HI has not been prevented from delivering essential humanitarian aid since February 2025. Only a few hospitals remain capable of providing care.</p>

<p>Violence has also surged in the West Bank. Between 7 October 2023 and 15 March 2026, over 1,000 Palestinians were killed in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and over 30,000 were displaced by ongoing military operations and escalating settler violence.</p>

<ul>

	<li>Date the programme opened: 1996</li>
</ul>

						<h2><!--StartFragment -->Crisis in the Holy Land</h2>

<p paraeid="{a36cbfaf-7f88-45f7-946d-3a929a0bc2dd}{51}" paraid="888114010">Across Gaza, life remains defined by uncertainty. Many families are still living in tents and overcrowded shelters, where the summer heat, a lack of clean water and inadequate sanitation make even everyday tasks difficult.  </p>

<p paraeid="{a36cbfaf-7f88-45f7-946d-3a929a0bc2dd}{53}" paraid="1040860012">Continued conflict is a constant source of stress, damaging critical infrastructure—including electrical lines and water systems—and uprooting thousands of people, some for a second or third time. Restrictions on humanitarian access mean many families are still waiting for food, medicine and other essentials.  </p>

						<h2>CRS and Partner Response</h2>

<p>In response, CRS and our partners have provided lifesaving assistance to more than 1.7 million people across Gaza and the West Bank, including food, shelter, water, cash assistance, and social and emotional support.  </p>

<p>In Gaza, CRS is the second largest non-governmental organization importing humanitarian supplies—helping ensure critical aid reaches families despite severe access constraints. CRS has provided food, shelter, bedding, solar lamps, water, sanitation support and mental health services to families affected by the crisis, while also helping communities begin to recover through a cash-for-work program, small business grants and home gardens.  </p>

<p>As in Gaza, CRS is providing many of the same core forms of assistance in the West Bank, including cash assistance, shelter support, essential household items, mental health services and livelihoods programming. These efforts help families forced from their homes or struggling with deepening economic hardship to meet their immediate needs while beginning to rebuild their lives.  </p>

<p>To date, CRS has provided emergency cash assistance to approximately 22,450 people, helping families buy food, medicine and other essentials. CRS has also helped approximately 2,500 displaced households with bedding, blankets, mattresses, kitchen supplies and other essential items.  </p>

<p>Today, CRS is piloting an innovative shelter program in Tulkarm in the northern West Bank, where repairs to rental homes are exchanged for rent-free housing for displaced families for a set period. At the same time, CRS is expanding trauma-informed mental health support and strengthening local organizations so they can better identify, refer and care for people experiencing distress.  </p>

<p>In Area C, where restrictions on land, water, construction and movement make it difficult for families to earn a living or recover from crisis, CRS is testing practical, climate-resilient solutions that help communities move forward. These efforts include helping families grow food using less water, improving access to water for homes and farms, and supporting women- and youth-led small businesses so households can earn income and better provide for their families.</p>

<h3>Program Priorities</h3>

						<h2>CRS’ History in Jerusalem, West Bank and Gaza</h2>

<p>CRS has supported vulnerable communities in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza since 1961 and has maintained a continuous presence in the Gaza Strip since 1984. For decades, CRS has worked alongside communities, the local Catholic Church and trusted partners, enabling rapid, flexible, and impactful responses in Gaza’s fast changing and complex environment.  </p>

<p>CRS currently has 130 staff members, including 103 based in Gaza, and maintains offices in East Jerusalem, Ramallah, Bethlehem, as well as north and south Gaza. CRS and its partners support programs that address the full spectrum of needs by strengthening local response capacity, providing lifesaving assistance and building on local systems to help communities manage recovery.  </p>

<p>The Church’s historical and cultural presence in Gaza and the broader region is more vital than ever, and CRS’ long-standing partners are deeply rooted in the life of the community and trusted across religious and social lines. </p>

						<h5>Your compassion helps people in need around the world.</h5><div class="content-montlhy hidden"><h5><strong>As little as 40¢ a day can make a difference.</strong></h5><p>Join Catholic Relief Services’ Footsteps in Faith monthly giving program, along with thousands of committed Catholics dedicated to serving people in need. When you give monthly, you bring immediate and long-term support to people in need around the world.</p></div><div class="content-one-time d-block"><p><strong>Every gift you give helps a child thrive, brings hope to a family and rebuilds a community.</strong></p><p>When you give, you help provide food to young children so they can study hard in school. You help prevent trafficking and provide welcome kits for survivors. You help mothers and babies around the world receive nutritional care and health exams.</p></div><div class="collapsible"><div class="content-one-time d-block"><p>When you give, refugees find safety and receive emergency assistance and trauma counseling. Farmers learn innovative ways to plant and grow crops despite drought or disease. And women find dignity in opportunities for savings and training.</p><p><strong>You can make an immediate lifesaving difference and give hope to children, mothers and fathers around the world.</strong></p><p>For more than 80 years, CRS has been providing expertise and compassion to the most vulnerable of our sisters and brothers in more than 90 countries. And it's because of you.</p><p><strong>We can't do this lifesaving work without your help. </strong>Please make a generous gift today and fill out the secure form to make a one-time donation.</p><p>Looking to donate securities, or make a DAF or QCD gift? We’ve made it even easier. <a href="https://www.freewill.com/smartgiving/crs?product=daf&utm_source=partner&utm_medium=website&utm_campaign=202408_crs_MainPage_DonationForm_donatepg">Complete your gift today.</a></p></div><div class="content-montlhy hidden"><p>For more than 80 years, Catholic Relief Services has responded immediately when emergencies occur—sometimes before they are reported by the media—thanks to you.</p><p><strong>By committing a monthly gift to your sisters and brothers around the world, you’ll be at the forefront of giving comfort and aid to families affected by disasters.</strong></p><h3>When you join Footsteps in Faith, you:</h3><ul><li data-list-item-id="e544d1c7d6c74b5ccfb8f14d746ff601f">Make an impact by protecting families in need.</li><li data-list-item-id="e4917b50ab9d81f6213cc687dc75ca580">Rush aid to people during emergencies.</li><li data-list-item-id="e13bab303602188e22649f7fa7480d16e">Help provide long-term care effectively and efficiently.</li><li data-list-item-id="ee23854eadd78e00109d71bf7c15d1d99">Enjoy ease of giving—join once and that’s it!</li><li data-list-item-id="e9bb0a4b4da25df27709826c34015d1fc">Receive updates about the people you help.</li><li data-list-item-id="e12f7ab45702675fb0e989b8f8f1f5cb5">Live your faith in an extraordinary way.</li></ul><hr><p><strong>To give by phone, please call:</strong> 877-435-7277.<br>Already a recurring donor and want to update your gift?<br>Simply call us at the number above or fill out this form again with your new desired gift amount, credit card or bank account information.<br>Questions? Email us at <a class="obfuscated-email" data-email="Z3JvLnNyY0BzZWNpdnJlc3Jvbm9k" href="mailto:donorservices@crs.org" data-processed="true"><span class="email-text">donorservices@crs.org</span></a>.</p><p><strong>Did you know?</strong><br>Automatic transfers are the fastest way to put your gifts to work. Occupied Palestinian Territory

homekeyboard_arrow_right Occupied Palestinian Territory

Since 2007, Acted has supported crisis-affected communities across the occupied Palestinian territory through humanitarian response, early recovery and longer-term resilience programming. Its established presence, operational capacity and local networks enable rapid and flexible action as needs and access conditions evolve. Drawing on expertise in site management, shelter, WASH, food security, nutrition, livelihoods and cash assistance, Acted delivers integrated, area-based support shaped by community priorities and evidence. Community engagement and feedback help Acted identify gaps, adapt its programming and reach underserved communities, while partnerships with local organisations and other humanitarian actors strengthen coordination and local ownership. Guided by its 3ZERO vision, Acted links immediate assistance with inclusive and environmentally responsible recovery.

Since October 2023, the situation has deteriorated significantly in the occupied Palestinian territory. The crisis in Gaza has resulted in 73,407 reported fatalities and 174,335 injuries as of August 2026, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. OCHA’s 2026 Flash Appeal states that Gaza’s entire population of 2.1 million people is experiencing food insecurity and requires emergency food assistance. WASH Cluster monitoring found moderate-to-high water insecurity among 90% of assessed households, while the Shelter Cluster estimates that around 1.5 million people require shelter and essential household items. The situation has also deteriorated across the West Bank: between January 2025 and July 2026, OCHA documented more than 3,200 settler attacks resulting in Palestinian casualties and/or property damage, while demolitions displaced around 3,000 Palestinians. Damage to water and agricultural infrastructure, compounded by climate pressures, is further undermining livelihoods and resilience.

Total population (Worldometer 2026) 5.7 million
Poverty rate (Worldometer 2025) 58.4%
Unemployment rate (PCBS, December 2025) 51% (2025)
People in need of humanitarian assistance (OCHA 2026) 3.6 million

Acted in the Occupied Palestinian Territory

In the occupied Palestinian territory, Acted works across humanitarian response, early recovery and development to address vulnerabilities driven by conflict, displacement, movement restrictions, economic marginalization and climate stress.

Through its 3ZERO vision, Acted addresses these challenges through three interconnected priorities. Under Zero Poverty, Acted meets urgent needs while helping restore livelihoods and essential services disrupted by conflict, demolitions and displacement. Under Zero Exclusion, it promotes community participation, maintains accessible feedback mechanisms and works with Palestinian organizations and institutions to reach underserved groups and ensure assistance reflects local priorities. Under Zero Carbon, Acted responds to growing pressure on water, land and energy resources by rehabilitating essential infrastructure and promoting water-efficient systems, renewable energy and climate-smart livelihoods.

This approach is adapted to the distinct realities of Gaza and the West Bank. In Gaza, Acted’s area-based and site management expertise supports coordinated assistance and community-led solutions for displaced people, returnees and host communities. In the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, rapid emergency assistance is complemented by efforts to restore livelihoods, strengthen local institutions and build climate resilience. Across the oPt, Acted brings together operational capacity, local knowledge and partnerships to help communities recover, prepare for future shocks and shape sustainable solutions.

    Privacy

    This website uses cookies so that we can provide you with the best user experience possible. Cookie information is stored in your browser and performs functions such as recognising you when you return to our website and helping our team to understand which sections of the website you find most interesting and useful, so we can improve your browsing experience and the information made available.

    You can adjust all of your cookie settings by navigating the tabs on the left hand side.

    According to the French law N• 78-17 of 6 January 1978 on computing, data and liberties (CNIL), all users who has deposited nominal information either directly or indirectly, may ask for the submission of this nominal information through a request to Acted Data Protection Officer either by email or in written to Acted DPO, 33, rue Godot de Mauroy, 75009 Paris, France – and have them edited or suppressed.

    Terms and conditions of the Acted website are available here.

    Manage Your Cookies

    Enabling the Strictly Necessary Cookie allows us to save your preferences for cookie settings and ease your browsing experience with us.

    Google Analytics

    This website uses Google Analytics to collect anonymous information such as the number of visitors to the site, and the most popular pages.

    Keeping this cookie enabled helps us to improve our website.

    Acted Cookie Policy

    While on our website, cookie files may be deposited on your terminal (computer, smartphone, or any other terminal).

    Cookie files are needed for the smooth running of the website and allows the drawing of analytical statistics to improve our contents. Data collected to this end is strictly anonymous.

    Links to external social networks on the Acted website do not include tracing systems and will not share any personal data.

  1. 01

قصتنا

أسست جمعية نجوم الأمل لتمكين النساء ذوات الإعاقة علي يد نخبة من النساء ذوات الاعاقة عام 2007، إيمانًا منهن بالحاجة الملحة لوجود منظمة تتفرد في تلبية احتياجات النساء والفتيات ذوات الإعاقة؛ نظرًا لحجم التمييز والعنف المضاعف عليهن بفعل كونهن نساء من جهة وذوات إعاقة من جهة أخرى.

 

تعمل الجمعية على إلغاء العنف الواقع على النساء ذوات الإعاقة بتقدميها خدمات تتنوع بين التوعية، والارشاد، التمكين ل:

1- النساء والفتيات ذوات الإعاقة أنفسهن وذويهن.

2- صناع القرار على المستوى السياسي والمؤسسي.

تأسست الجمعية عام 1993م كجمعية خيرية تقوم برعاية وتأهيل ذوي الاحتياجات الخاصة، وتسعى جاهدة لتعزيز دورهم في المجتمع وتحقيق الاندماج الكامل.

فيديو
١١ نوفمبر ٢٠٢٦

الجمعية الفلسطينية لتأهيل المعاقين تُطلق مبادرة إنسانية لحلاقة وتجهيز الأطفال من ذوي الإعاقة

وثقت الجمعية الفلسطينية لتأهيل المعاقين عبر مقطع مرئي جديد جانباً من فعاليات مبادرتها الميدانية المخصصة لحلاقة وتجهيز الأطفال من ذوي الإعاقة. وتهدف المبادرة إلى تقديم خدمات العناية الشخصية للأطفال في بيئة صديقة ومحفزة تراعي احتياجاتهم الخاصة وتخفف الأعباء النفسية والاقتصادية عن كاهل عائلاتهم، وذلك بمشاركة نخبة من المتطوعين المختصين بكوادر الجمعية. وتؤكد الجمعية أن هذه المبادرة تأتي ضمن سلسلة من البرامج والخدمات التأهيلية الموجهة لدعم الأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة وتعزيز دمجهم ومساندتهم في المجتمع بكل كرامة واهتمام. [شاهد الفيديو أعلاه] 🔻 للمساهمة في رعاية البرامج والمشاريع القادمة للأطفال، يمكنكم التبرع مباشرة عبر صفحة المبادرات https://pardgaza.ps/donate.

اقرأ التفاصيل
فيديو
٢٦ أكتوبر ٢٠٢٦

زيتونُنا هُويّتنا وفنُّنا حكايةُ انتمائنا: إبداعات الطلاب في مادة التربية الفنية

توثيق نتاجات مادة التربية الفنية لطلاب الجمعية وترسيخ الهوية والتراث الفلسطيني من خلال الرسم. تحت شعار «زيتونُنا هُويّتنا… وفنُّنا حكايةُ انتمائنا»، نظمت الجمعية نشاطاً فنياً ضمن مادة التربية الفنية بالتزامن مع موسم قطف الزيتون. هدف النشاط إلى إتاحة المساحة للطلاب للتعبير عن مشاعرهم وارتباطهم بأرضهم وتراثهم عبر أدوات الرسم والألوان، لترسيخ المفاهيم الوطنية والجمالية في نفوسهم. ندعوكم لمشاهدة المقطع التوثيقي المرفق للاطلاع على إبداعات رسامينا الصغار.

اقرأ التفاصيل

٥ أكتوبر ٢٠٢٦

ورشة تدريبية للمعلمات بالتعاون بين الجمعية الفلسطينية و"الأونروا" حول آليات الاكتشاف المبكر والإحالة

نظمت الجمعية الفلسطينية، بالتنسيق والتعاون مع وكالة غوث وتشغيل اللاجئين الفلسطينيين (الأونروا)، ورشة عمل تدريبية استهدفت المعلمات؛ بهدف تعزيز قدراتهن على التحديد والاكتشاف المبكر للحالات الحرجـة التي تتطلب تدخلاً متخصصاً، وتوضيح مسارات ومعايير الإحالة المعتمدة للتعامل معها وفق الأصول والبرامج المعمول بها في الأونروا.

أعمالنا الميدانية

برامج ومشاريع الجمعية

نسعى من خلال مجموعة متكاملة من البرامج والمشاريع لتلبية احتياجات الأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة وتوفير الرعاية الشاملة لهم ولأسرهم.

برنامج المدرسة - التأهيل المهني

تدريب مهني متخصص يهدف إلى تمكين الأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة من اكتساب مهارات عملية تساعدهم على الاستقلالية والاندماج في سوق العمل.

اقرأ المزيد

برنامج المدرسة - التعليم الأكاديمي

برنامج تعليمي شامل يوفر تعليماً أكاديمياً متميزاً للطلاب ذوي الاحتياجات الخاصة وفق منهاج وزارة التربية والتعليم الفلسطينية.

اقرأ المزيد

مركز تعزيز القدرات

برامج متنوعة لتطوير المهارات الحياتية والاجتماعية والنفسية للأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة وأسرهم من خلال ورش عمل وأنشطة تفاعلية.

اقرأ المزيد

البرنامج الخارجي

خدمات تأهيلية منزلية ومجتمعية تصل إلى الأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة في منازلهم ومجتمعاتهم المحلية لضمان وصول الخدمة للجميع.

اقرأ المزيد

وحدة العلاج الطبيعي

خدمات علاج طبيعي متخصصة تقدمها كوادر مؤهلة باستخدام أحدث التقنيات والأجهزة لتحسين الحركة والوظائف الجسدية.

اقرأ المزيد

برامج الدعم الأسري

دعم نفسي واجتماعي لأسر الأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة من خلال جلسات إرشادية ومجموعات دعم لتعزيز قدرتهم على الرعاية والتعامل.

اقرأ المزيد
المشروع الأبرز حالياً

مشروع دعم وتوفير احتياجات المعاقين في قطاع غزة

يعد هذا المشروع استجابةً عاجلةً وضروريةً للظروف الصعبة التي يمر بها قطاع غزة، حيث يسعى لتلبية الاحتياجات الأساسية والطبية لذوي الإعاقة الذين يواجهون تحديات مضاعفة في الوصول إلى الخدمات الأساسية.

التقارير السنوية

اطلع على تقاريرنا السنوية لمعرفة المزيد عن إنجازاتنا وأنشطتنا المالية والإدارية. نحن نؤمن بالشفافية كقيمة أساسية في عملنا.

التقرير الإداري السنوي للعامين 2025

يستعرض هذا التقرير الإداري السنوي للعامين 2025 مسيرة عمل وبرامج الجمعية الفلسطينية لتأهيل المعاقين في قطاع غزة، ويوضح أثر الظروف الاستثنائية وفترة الحرب على الخدمات، مع التركيز على مشروع التعليم والدعم الشامل للأطفال اللاجئين ذوي الإعاقة المنفذ بالشراكة مع وكالة الغوث الدولية (الأونروا).

تابع التغطيات الإخبارية الشاملة، والتقارير المرئية والمصورة لكافة البرامج والأنشطة التي تنفذها الجمعية.

١١ نوفمبر ٢٠٢٦

الجمعية الفلسطينية لتأهيل المعاقين تُطلق مبادرة إنسانية لحلاقة وتجهيز الأطفال من ذوي الإعاقة

وثقت الجمعية الفلسطينية لتأهيل المعاقين عبر مقطع مرئي جديد جانباً من فعاليات مبادرتها الميدانية المخصصة لحلاقة وتجهيز الأطفال من ذوي الإعاقة. وتهدف المبادرة إلى تقديم خدمات العناية الشخصية للأطفال في بيئة صديقة ومحفزة تراعي احتياجاتهم الخاصة وتخفف الأعباء النفسية والاقتصادية عن كاهل عائلاتهم، وذلك بمشاركة نخبة من المتطوعين المختصين بكوادر الجمعية. وتؤكد الجمعية أن هذه المبادرة تأتي ضمن سلسلة من البرامج والخدمات التأهيلية الموجهة لدعم الأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة وتعزيز دمجهم ومساندتهم في المجتمع بكل كرامة واهتمام. [شاهد الفيديو أعلاه] 🔻 للمساهمة في رعاية البرامج والمشاريع القادمة للأطفال، يمكنكم التبرع مباشرة عبر صفحة المبادرات https://pardgaza.ps/donate.

اقرأ التفاصيل
فيديو
٢٦ أكتوبر ٢٠٢٦

زيتونُنا هُويّتنا وفنُّنا حكايةُ انتمائنا: إبداعات الطلاب في مادة التربية الفنية

توثيق نتاجات مادة التربية الفنية لطلاب الجمعية وترسيخ الهوية والتراث الفلسطيني من خلال الرسم. تحت شعار «زيتونُنا هُويّتنا… وفنُّنا حكايةُ انتمائنا»، نظمت الجمعية نشاطاً فنياً ضمن مادة التربية الفنية بالتزامن مع موسم قطف الزيتون. هدف النشاط إلى إتاحة المساحة للطلاب للتعبير عن مشاعرهم وارتباطهم بأرضهم وتراثهم عبر أدوات الرسم والألوان، لترسيخ المفاهيم الوطنية والجمالية في نفوسهم. ندعوكم لمشاهدة المقطع التوثيقي المرفق للاطلاع على إبداعات رسامينا الصغار.

اقرأ التفاصيل
فيديو
٢٥ أكتوبر ٢٠٢٦

طلاب الجمعية يشاركون في "موسم قطف الزيتون": ترسيخ للهوية وتعزيز لروح العمل الجماعي

ضمن إطار أنشطتها المجتمعية والتربوية الهادفة، نظمت الجمعية نشاطاً ميدانياً ممتعاً لطلابها لمشاركتهم في "موسم قطف الزيتون"، وذلك بهدف تعزيز ارتباط الأجيال القادمة بأرضهم وتراثهم الأصيل. وتخلل النشاط العديد من الفقرات التفاعلية والتعليمية التي غرسنا من خلالها قيم التعاون، والعمل الجماعي، وتنمية روح المسؤولية لدى الطلاب أثناء مشاركتهم المباشرة في عمليات القطاف وسط أجواء ملؤها الفرح والنشاط. نتوجه بالشكر الجزيل لكل من ساهم في إنجاح هذا اليوم المتميز من طلاب، ومشرفين، وداعمين. وندعوكم لمشاهدة الفيديو التوثيقي المرفق للتعرف على أبرز لحظات النشاط.

وكالة الأونروا UNRWA تنفذ زيارة إشرافية ومتابعة ميدانية للجمعية الفلسطينية لتأهيل المعاقين بغزة

استقبلت الجمعية الفلسطينية لتأهيل المعاقين - غزة، وفداً من وكالة غوث وتشغيل اللاجئين الفلسطينيين (الأونروا) في زيارة إشرافية ومتابعة ميدانية لسير العمل والخدمات التي تقدمها الجمعية. وهدفت الزيارة إلى الاطلاع عن كثب على البرامج والخدمات المقدمة للأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة، ومتابعة آليات التنفيذ، وضمان جودة الخدمات المقدمة للمستفيدين. وتثمن الجمعية هذه الزيارة الكريمة التي تعكس عمق الشراكة والتعاون المستمر مع وكالة الأونروا، وتؤكد التزامها بمواصلة العمل وتطوير خدماتها بما يخدم أبناء شعبنا. ورشة تدريبية للمعلمات بالتعاون بين الجمعية الفلسطينية و"الأونروا" حول آليات الاكتشاف المبكر والإحالة

نظمت الجمعية الفلسطينية، بالتنسيق والتعاون مع وكالة غوث وتشغيل اللاجئين الفلسطينيين (الأونروا)، ورشة عمل تدريبية استهدفت المعلمات؛ بهدف تعزيز قدراتهن على التحديد والاكتشاف المبكر للحالات الحرجـة التي تتطلب تدخلاً متخصصاً، وتوضيح مسارات ومعايير الإحالة المعتمدة للتعامل معها وفق الأصول والبرامج المعمول بها في الأونروا.

الجمعية الفلسطينية لتأهيل المعاقين تكرّم الأستاذ سعيد عدنان الأستاذ تقديرًا لجهوده في دعم الأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة

كرّمت الجمعية الفلسطينية لتأهيل المعاقين الأستاذ/ سعيد عدنان الأستاذ تقديرًا لجهوده في دعم الأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة والفئات المهمشة، ضمن الشراكة مع برنامج الأغذية العالمي (WFP). كما عبّرت الجمعية عن خالص شكرها لمعالي وزيرة التنمية الاجتماعية الدكتورة/ سماح حمد، وللدكتور/ رمزي السويركي، منسق برنامج الأغذية العالمي، تقديرًا لجهودهما في دعم العمل الإغاثي والاجتماعي والإنساني في قطاع غزة.

لأن الابتسامة تبدأ بالدعم... ولأن كل طفل يحمل بداخله قدرات تستحق الرعاية والاهتمام. 💙

لأن الابتسامة تبدأ بالدعم... ولأن كل طفل يحمل بداخله قدرات تستحق الرعاية والاهتمام. 💙 نشارككم رسالة شكر صادقة من أحد أطفال الجمعية الفلسطينية لتأهيل المعاقين، تعبيراً عن الامتنان لكل من يساهم في دعم مسيرتنا الإنسانية ورسالتنا في التأهيل والتمكين. في الجمعية نؤمن بأن الدعم الحقيقي يصنع فرقاً، وأن كل خطوة صغيرة نحو تمكين أطفالنا هي خطوة نحو مستقبل أكثر أملاً. كل الشكر والتقدير لكل الداعمين والشركاء الذين يقفون معنا في خدمة أبنائنا وبناء قدراتهم. الجمعية الفلسطينية لتأهيل المعاقين Palestinian Association for Rehabilitation of the Disabled (PARD) 🌐 https://pardgaza.ps

٢١ يوليو ٢٠٢٦

حقيبة أمل... لابتسامة طفل: عندما يتحول العطاء إلى فرحة وأمل

لم تكن الفعالية مجرد توزيع للحقائب، بل كانت رسالة محبة ودعم ونبضاً بالأمل. بين طيات كل حقيبة قدمناها، أودعنا تشجيعاً وقسماً صادقاً يقول لأطفالنا بكل حب: "نحن معكم". لقد أضاءت عيون الأطفال المكان بفرحة لا تُقدر بثمن، وعلمونا اليوم درساً عميقاً في الحياة؛ أن الاختلاف بيننا هو نعمة تُثري إنسانيتنا، وأن العطاء عندما ينبع بصدق من القلب، يجد طريقه المباشر إلى القلب. 🎬 شاهدوا الفيديو أعلاه لتعيشوا معنا أجمل لحظات الأمل والفرح. #حقيبة_أمل ، #ابتسامة_طفل ، #عمل_إنساني ، #مبادرة_مجتمعية ، #فرحة_الأطفال ، #دعم_الأطفال ، #فيديو_ملهم

في تقرير خاص لصحيفة فلسطين، تستعرض مديرة الجمعية الفلسطينية لتأهيل المعاقين، أ. محاسن الحلبي، حجم الدمار الهائل الذي لحق بالجمعية جراء العدوان الإسرائيلي المستمر على قطاع غزة. التقرير يسلط الضوء على تدمير البنية التحتية، واستشهاد 4 معلمات، وتوقف الخدمات التأهيلية والتعليمية التي استفاد منها مئات الأطفال ذوي الإعاقة على مدار ثلاثة عقود، ويكشف عن جهود الجمعية الحالية لاستئناف عملها من وسط الركام وبإمكانيات محدودة جداً.

<style>
:root {
    /* ---------- الألوان الدلالية ---------- */
    --ui-primary: #187FCC;              /* أساسي — أزرق SDF (HR يعيد تعريفه تركوازياً) */
    --ui-primary-rgb: 24, 127, 204;
    --ui-primary-hover: #1570b8;
    --ui-primary-subtle: rgba(var(--ui-primary-rgb), .10);
    --ui-on-primary: #ffffff;

    --ui-secondary: #1CB7B3;            /* ثانوي — تركواز SDF */
    --ui-secondary-rgb: 28, 183, 179;

    --ui-success: #16a34a;
    --ui-success-rgb: 22, 163, 74;
    --ui-success-text: #15803d;
    --ui-warning: #D26F0D;
    --ui-warning-rgb: 210, 111, 13;
    --ui-warning-text: #b45309;
    --ui-danger: #dc2626;
    --ui-danger-rgb: 220, 38, 38;
    --ui-danger-text: #b91c1c;
    --ui-info: #0ea5e9;
    --ui-info-rgb: 14, 165, 233;
    --ui-info-text: #0369a1;

    --ui-bg: #f8fafc;                   /* خلفية الصفحة والأقسام الهادئة */
    --ui-surface: #ffffff;              /* البطاقات والجداول */
    --ui-border: #e2e8f0;
    --ui-border-subtle: #f1f5f9;

    --ui-text: #0f172a;
    --ui-text-secondary: #475569;
    --ui-text-muted: #64748b;          /* أدنى تباين مسموح لنص (4.7:1 على الأبيض) */

    /* ---------- الخط ---------- */
    --ui-font: 'Rubik', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif;
    --ui-fs-xs: 12px;     /* أصغر نص مسموح: شارات، تسميات ثانوية */
    --ui-fs-sm: 13px;     /* تسميات الحقول، رؤوس الجداول */
    --ui-fs-base: 14px;   /* جسم النص (15px على الموبايل عبر --ui-fs-body) */
    --ui-fs-md: 16px;     /* عناوين البطاقات */
    --ui-fs-lg: 20px;     /* عنوان الصفحة، أرقام الإحصاءات */
    --ui-fs-xl: 24px;
    --ui-fs-2xl: 32px;
    --ui-fs-body: var(--ui-fs-base);
    --ui-fw-normal: 400;
    --ui-fw-medium: 500;
    --ui-fw-semibold: 600;
    --ui-fw-bold: 700;
    --ui-lh: 1.6;

    /* ---------- الزوايا والظلال ---------- */
    --ui-radius-sm: 8px;    /* أزرار، حقول، شارات */
    --ui-radius-md: 12px;   /* بطاقات */
    --ui-radius-lg: 16px;   /* حاويات كبيرة، نوافذ */
    --ui-radius-pill: 999px;
    --ui-shadow-sm: 0 1px 3px rgba(15, 23, 42, .06);
    --ui-shadow-md: 0 6px 20px rgba(15, 23, 42, .08);

    /* ---------- المسافات (مضاعفات 4px) ---------- */
    --ui-space-1: 4px;
    --ui-space-2: 8px;
    --ui-space-3: 12px;
    --ui-space-4: 16px;
    --ui-space-5: 20px;
    --ui-space-6: 24px;
    --ui-space-8: 32px;

    /* ---------- التفاعل ---------- */
    --ui-touch: 44px;                   /* أدنى هدف لمس على الموبايل */
    --ui-focus-ring: 0 0 0 3px rgba(var(--ui-primary-rgb), .28);
    --ui-transition: 150ms ease;
}

/* الموبايل (< 768px): جسم النص 15px */
@media (max-width: 767.98px) {
    :root { --ui-fs-body: 15px; }
}

/* الوضع الداكن: الأسطح والنصوص فقط؛ الألوان الدلالية ثابتة */
[data-bs-theme="dark"] {
    --ui-bg: #041324;

    --ui-border: rgba(255, 255, 255, .10);
    --ui-border-subtle: rgba(255, 255, 255, .06);

    --ui-text-secondary: #cbd5e1;
    --ui-text-muted: #94a3b8;
    --ui-success-text: #4ade80;
    --ui-warning-text: #fbbf24;
    --ui-danger-text: #f87171;
    --ui-info-text: #38bdf8;
}
